# voxy

Facade for voice generation: speech synthesis in any voice, on any service, plus cloning and designing voices.

To install:	`pip install voxy` (add `'voxy[elevenlabs]'`, `'voxy[aix]'` or `'voxy[fal]'` for those services). torch is not installed by default: the local CSM model and tensor helpers (`cleanup_audio`, `generate_speech`) need `'voxy[local]'`, and Whisper transcription `'voxy[transcription]'`; the local backends that run in their own environments (kokoro, f5tts, …) need neither. The part-of-speech heteronym detector (`voxy.speechtext.pos_detector`) needs `'voxy[pos]'` plus `python -m spacy download fr_core_news_sm`. The LLM proposer (`voxy.speechtext.llm_detector`) uses `'voxy[aix]'` unless you pass `chat=`.

```python
import voxy

voxy.text_to_speech("Hello!", voice="ada").save(
    "hi.mp3"
)  # a named voice from the library
voxy.text_to_speech(
    "A quick draft.", voice="Daniel", backend="say"
)  # free local voice (macOS)
voxy.list_voices()  # our named voices
voxy.list_voices("elevenlabs")  # a service's voices
```

Backends: `elevenlabs` (cloning, voice design, TTS), `say` (macOS, offline), `aix` (OpenAI voices and other LiteLLM providers), `fal` (fal.ai models via falaw), `kokoro` (local stock voices, CPU, no key; see below), `voicestudio` (local text-described voices, `voxy[voicestudio]`), `csm` (local Sesame CSM-1B). Register more with `voxy.register_speech_model(name, factory)`.

Command line: `python -m voxy voices [--backend X]` and `python -m voxy speak "text" --voice ada -o out.mp3`.

## Designing a voice from a description

```python
model = voxy.get_speech_model("elevenlabs")
line = (
    "Once upon a time, in a village at the edge of a very old forest, there lived a "
    "baker who could hear the bread singing as it rose."
)  # 100-1000 characters
previews = model.design_voice_previews("a warm, slow, elderly storyteller", text=line)
for i, p in enumerate(previews):
    p.save(f"preview_{i}.mp3")  # listen, then pick one
voxy.design_from_description(
    "storyteller", "a warm, slow, elderly storyteller", preview=previews[1]
)
```

Change the voice of a recording (speech to speech, ElevenLabs): the words, timing and intonation stay the recording’s, the voice becomes the target’s. A correction can be spoken by anyone and come out in the narrator’s voice:

```python
voxy.speech_to_speech("my_take.wav", voice="ada").save("ada_take.mp3")
```

## Features

- Voice cloning from audio samples
- High-quality speech synthesis
- Flexible input formats (file paths, bytes, streams, tensors)
- Audio cleanup utilities
- Automatic audio transcription (using Whisper)
- Plugin architecture for different speech models

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.10+
- PyTorch and TorchAudio
- CUDA-compatible GPU (recommended)
- FFmpeg for audio processing

### Install at least one model

#### Example: the CSM Model

The intention is to make `voxy` into a plugin-enabled facade, where you can chose your
own engine (for voice cloning, voice synthesis, etc.).
But for now, we just support, what seems to be the best open-source model out there
(at the time of writing this):
[Sesame AI Lab’s](https://www.sesame.com/research/crossing_the_uncanny_valley_of_voice)
CSM model. It’s just that, well, they did an amazing job at the model, but a terrible one
(so far) for the python interface – which is what inspired me to develop `voxy`
in the first place.

Follow the instructions in the [CSM repository](https://github.com/SesameAILabs/csm)
to install the CSM model and its dependencies.

Try [the csm spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/sesame/csm-1b) where you can try various functionalities of csm.

## Quick Start

### Basic Usage

```python
from voxy import create_speech_model

# Create a speech model
model = create_speech_model(model_type="csm")

# Generate speech with default voice
audio = model.generate_speech(
    text="Hello, this is a test of the CSM speech model.", output_path="output.wav"
)
```

### Voice Cloning

```python
from voxy import create_speech_model

# Create a speech model
model = create_speech_model(model_type="csm")

# Clone a voice from an audio file
voice_profile = model.clone_voice(
    audio_input="sample_voice.wav",
    transcript="This is a sample of my voice for cloning purposes.",
)

# Generate speech with the cloned voice
audio = model.generate_speech(
    text="This is my cloned voice speaking. Isn't it amazing?",
    voice_profile=voice_profile,
    output_path="cloned_voice.wav",
)
```

### Automatic Transcription

```python
from voxy import create_speech_model

# Create a speech model
model = create_speech_model(model_type="csm")

# Clone a voice with automatic transcription
voice_profile = model.clone_voice(
    audio_input="sample_voice.wav",
    # No transcript provided, will use automatic transcription
)

# Generate speech with the cloned voice
audio = model.generate_speech(
    text="This voice was cloned using automatic transcription.",
    voice_profile=voice_profile,
    output_path="auto_transcribed_voice.wav",
)
```

### Flexible Input Formats

The module supports various input formats:

```python
# From file path
voice_profile1 = model.clone_voice(
    audio_input="sample_voice.wav", transcript="Text transcript."
)

# From bytes
with open("sample_voice.wav", "rb") as f:
    audio_bytes = f.read()
voice_profile2 = model.clone_voice(
    audio_input=audio_bytes, transcript="Text transcript."
)

# From file object
with open("sample_voice.wav", "rb") as f:
    voice_profile3 = model.clone_voice(audio_input=f, transcript="Text transcript.")

# From tensor
import torch
import torchaudio

audio_tensor, sample_rate = torchaudio.load("sample_voice.wav")
voice_profile4 = model.clone_voice(
    audio_input=audio_tensor, transcript="Text transcript."
)
```

### ElevenLabs backend

Install with `pip install 'voxy[elevenlabs]'` and set `ELEVEN_API_KEY` or `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` (checked in that order), or pass `api_key=`.

```python
from voxy import create_speech_model

model = create_speech_model("elevenlabs")

# Instant voice clone: one sample or several (paths, bytes, file-likes, tensors), at most 25 files.
# ElevenLabs recommends 1-2 minutes of clean single-speaker audio in total (at most ~3).
profile = model.clone_voice(["clip1.wav", "clip2.m4a"], name="my-voice")
print(profile.segment)  # the ElevenLabs voice_id

audio = model.generate_speech(
    "Hello from my cloned voice.", profile, output_path="hello.wav"
)

# Later sessions: rebuild the profile from the id, no re-upload.
profile = model.voice_profile("<voice_id>")
```

`generate_speech` returns a tensor for `pcm_*`/`wav_*` output formats (default `pcm_24000`); `synthesize_bytes` returns the raw payload in any format (e.g. `mp3_44100_128`). `delete_voice` removes a clone from the account. ElevenLabs requires that you have the right, and the voice owner’s consent, to clone a voice.

Live tests are opt-in: `VOXY_LIVE_ELEVENLABS=1` runs a short synthesis; adding `VOXY_LIVE_ELEVENLABS_SAMPLE=<audio you may clone>` also clones, speaks and deletes.

### A local stock voice (no service, no clip, no torch)

`kokoro` speaks in one of 54 stock voices (`af_heart`, `am_michael`, `bf_emma`, …) with Kokoro-82M (Apache-2.0) through kokoro-onnx, faster than realtime on a CPU. It runs in its own small environment, which `python -m voxy setup kokoro` builds (or the first call does); the model files (about 354 MB) are fetched from the Hugging Face hub on first use into `$VOXY_DATA_DIR/models/hf`, like every other local backend’s weights. Listing its voices needs neither. A voice’s first letter is its language (`a` American, `b` British, `f` French, `e` Spanish, `i` Italian, `p` Portuguese, `h` Hindi, `j` Japanese, `z` Chinese). It is meant for Linux hosts without a cloud key; on macOS the espeak-ng that kokoro-onnx bundles currently fails to find its data (thorwhalen/voxy#61), and `say` is the local voice there.

```python
voxy.text_to_speech("Hello.", "bf_emma", backend="kokoro", speed=1.1).save("hi.wav")
voxy.list_voices("kokoro")
```

### Correcting words in a recording

`voxy.replace_words` replaces a spoken phrase with a new one in the speaker’s voice: it finds the phrase in the recording’s ASR words, renders the new phrase (TTS in `voice=` by default, or any `render=`), cuts at the quietest moment near each end, matches the loudness of the speech it replaces (pauses excluded), crossfades, and checks that the new words are heard there and the old ones are gone. Pass `voice=` (the speaker’s voice) or `render=`.

```python
fixed = voxy.replace_words("narration.wav", "Anna Jones", "Anna Smith", voice="ada")
fixed.passed, fixed.checks  # True, [{'check': 'heard', 'passed': True, ...}]
fixed.save("narration-fixed.wav")
```

Replace the whole phrase around a word (first name and surname), not the word alone: the neighbouring sounds anticipate it. `old` is the phrase as ASR heard it.

### Local voice cloning (no service, CPU works)

Five local models clone a voice from one clean clip and its transcript: `voxcpm` (VoxCPM2), `qwen3tts` (Qwen3-TTS), `chatterbox`, `f5tts` (F5-TTS) and `xtts` (XTTS-v2). Each runs in its own Python environment, built on first use with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) under `$VOXY_DATA_DIR/envs/` (weights under `$VOXY_DATA_DIR/models/`), so their clashing torch/transformers pins never touch yours. Requirements: `uv` and `ffmpeg` on the PATH.

```python
import voxy
from voxy.local_clone import reference_profile

model = voxy.create_speech_model("voxcpm")  # or qwen3tts, chatterbox, f5tts, xtts
voice = reference_profile("ref.wav", "Exactly what the clip says.")
model.synthesize(chapter_text, voice, cfg_value=2.0).save("chapter1.wav")
model.close()  # free the model's memory
```

Long text is split into paragraphs and sentence-packed chunks, each spoken separately and joined with controlled pauses (`gap_ms=`, `paragraph_gap_ms=`). Model parameters are keyword arguments of `synthesize` (see `voxy.local_clone.local_backends()[name].params`); model options (a variant, a fine-tuned checkpoint) are keyword arguments of `create_speech_model`. Threads are capped at `$VOXY_NUM_THREADS` (default 8). Licences differ: F5-TTS and XTTS-v2 weights are non-commercial (XTTS needs `accept_licence=True`); VoxCPM2, Qwen3-TTS and Chatterbox are Apache-2.0/MIT.

Languages: VoxCPM2 (30 languages), Qwen3-TTS (10, pass `language="French"` etc.), XTTS-v2 (17, `language="fr"`) and Chatterbox with `variant="multilingual"` (23, `language="fr"`) speak beyond English; Chatterbox’s `original` and `turbo` variants and the F5-TTS base model are English (F5 also Chinese).

**Which backend?** [docs/benchmarks.md]() compares the cloning backends on published benchmarks (French and English accuracy, voice likeness rated by people, arenas, licence, price, watermark), with tables, charts and a link to every source. The data is `voxy/data/benchmarks.json`; `python -m voxy benchmarks docs/benchmarks.md` regenerates the tables and charts after you edit it.

```python
model = voxy.create_speech_model("chatterbox", variant="multilingual")
speech = model.synthesize("Bonjour à tous.", voice, language="fr")
```

```bash
python -m voxy setup voxcpm qwen3tts      # build environments ahead of time
python -m voxy prep ada tape1.m4a tape2.mp3 --language en
python -m voxy prep ada interview.m4a --speaker dominant   # drop the interviewer's voice
python -m voxy diagnose spec.json --out renders/first-listen --publish
```

**Reference preparation** (`voxy.refprep.prepare_reference`): converts any recording to mono WAV, denoises (`denoise=` `afftdn`, `anlmdn`, or `deepfilternet`, which lowers real room noise far more but builds its own torch environment on first use) and normalises loudness (ffmpeg), transcribes locally with Whisper (scribed’s faster-whisper backend) with word timings, cuts clips of 3-12 s at sentence boundaries, and scores each clip (signal-to-noise, clipping, level, ASR confidence, speaking rate). With `speaker=voxy.speakers.speaker_filter()` (`--speaker`) it keeps one voice: ECAPA speaker embeddings (SpeechBrain, in its own environment) decide each transcribed turn as a whole against the target’s voice print (the recording’s dominant voice by default, or `speakers.voice_print(clean_recordings)`), and interviewer questions, interjections such as “Yes.” and untranscribed “uh-huh”s never end up inside a clip. Clips and `manifest.jsonl` go to the voice’s samples store, which a run only ever adds to: running again (more recordings, or the same file re-cut) writes under fresh keys and keeps every earlier clip, its bytes and its manifest entry, so saved reference profiles stay valid; `refprep.forget(samples, source, run=None, dry_run=False)` is the one function that removes a source’s clips (`dry_run=True` lists what it would delete). `best_references(manifest)` picks reference clips and `voxy.finetune.export_dataset` writes training sets (LJSpeech or F5-TTS layout), both from each source’s latest run (`refprep.latest_runs`; `latest_only=False` for every run).

**Diagnosis pages** (`voxy.diagnosis`): render one text through a grid of models and parameters, then build one page with a player per variant, its parameters, generation time and real-time factor. Each variant has a stable ID (e.g. `VX-7KQ2`) derived from its configuration, not the text, so listeners can say “use VX-7KQ2” across pages and chapters; each listener can rate and annotate variants and copy their notes. A spec:

```json
{"title": "First listen", "text_file": "excerpt.txt", "voice": "ada", "n_references": 1,
 "grid": [{"backend": "voxcpm", "params": {"cfg_value": [1.5, 2.0, 2.5]}},
          {"backend": "chatterbox", "params": {"exaggeration": [0.3, 0.6]}}]}
```

Cards are titled with readable names (the backend, then the settings that vary, e.g. “Chatterbox 0.3”). For a page you share with other listeners, optional spec keys help: `references` (named clips, e.g. a raw and a denoised one, each with a `label`), `appendix` (reference name → a note: those variants go in a collapsed section at the end), `imported` (clips rendered elsewhere, such as a cloud service, with their `backend`, `label` and `audio_file`), `backend_notes`, `noindex`, and `notes_sink` + `page_url`, which save every rating, note, name and clip play as they happen to an [annoquest](https://github.com/i2mint/annoquest) server (`{"kind": "annoquest", "url": "/api/annoquest", "request": "<id>"}`). The page says so, and `annoquest-request.json` is written next to it for registering on that server; add `?reader=<name>` to the link you send each listener to tell them apart.

### Heteronyms: what to send, and checking what was said

Speech models misread words with two pronunciations (French *est* as the verb /ɛ/ or the noun /ɛst/, *plus*, *tous*, *fils*, the  *-ent* verbs), and a verse line’s capital makes it worse. An ASR check never sees it: Whisper writes “est” either way. Prepare the text, then audit the audio:

```python
from voxy.speechtext import prepare_speech_text
from voxy.pronounce import audit

text = prepare_speech_text(
    verse, keep={"Vous"}
).speech  # verse capitals lowercased, deliberate ones kept
# ... render `text` to take.wav with any backend ...
findings = audit(
    text, "take.wav", expected={"est": "verb"}
)  # voxy's French heteronym table by default
misread = [f for f in findings if f.ok is False]  # re-render these
```

voxy ships a short hand-made French table (`heteronym_readings("fr")`). For more, derive one from your copy of [Lexique](http://www.lexique.org) (voxy ships no Lexique data): `voxy.lexique.cached_lexique_heteronyms("Lexique383.tsv", min_frequency=1)` (derived once, then kept in voxy’s cache) returns the spellings Lexique gives more than one pronunciation, in the same `{word: {reading: IPA}}` shape, readings named by part of speech (or by lemma when two share one) and pronunciations that differ only by Lexique’s open/closed vowels or schwa folded into `name~variant`. Merge it under the hand-made table, `{**derived, **heteronym_readings("fr")}`: Lexique keeps one pronunciation per spelling, part of speech and lemma, and no liaison or variant readings, so *tous*, *os*, *six*, *dix*, *christ*, *lacs* and *fait* are not in it.

`audit` finds each flagged word in the render and scores its readings, written in IPA, as the whole phrase around it (neighbours written out by a bundled espeak-ng) with a wav2vec2 phoneme recogniser; both run in their own environment, built on first use. Expected readings come from `expected` (a mapping, or a function of each risk) or from a detector such as `voxy.speechtext.pos_detector()`. A heteronym elided onto a clitic that can precede its noun reading (French *l’Est*, *vent d’est*) is flagged and checked too; name it in the mapping by its clitic (`{"est": "verb", "l'est": "noun"}`), since `"est"` alone does not cover it. A mapping is checked whole up front: a key that is not a word of the readings table (a typo), or a reading that word does not have, raises a `ValueError` before any ASR, and `audit_verifier` raises it when built, before the first render; a detector’s proposal naming no reading is dropped with a warning. While rendering, `render_verified` scores the same way and re-renders a line whose word came out wrong; its one `verify=` seam, `(text, audio, line) -> findings`, defaults to `audit` on the line, occurrence by occurrence, elided forms included; pass `verify=audit_verifier(lines, readings=..., expected=..., detectors=...)` for `audit`’s own options. The older `checks=` (`checks_by_line`, `verify_words`) is a legacy adapter that matches words by spelling. `audit` takes `scoring=` (`"phrase"`, `"spot"` or `"crop"`), and all three take a `scorer=` (a name or a scorer from `phrase_scorer`/`spot_scorer`/`crop_scorer`, each carrying the margin it is calibrated for); cropping the word at its ASR times credits a neighbour’s /s/ or /t/ to the longer reading, so keep the default.

### The voice library: clone once, reuse by name

voxy keeps voice data in stores (`MutableMapping`s) under `$VOXY_DATA_DIR` (default `~/.local/share/voxy`): `voices/{name}.json` records (with each backend’s saved profile, e.g. the ElevenLabs `voice_id`), `samples/{name}/` (audio a clone is made from), `sources/{name}/` (raw media). Every library function takes its stores as arguments (`voices=`, `samples=`), so any `MutableMapping` (another folder, S3) can stand in.

```python
from voxy import samples_store, clone_from_samples, load_voice, create_speech_model

samples = samples_store("ada")
samples["clip1.wav"] = open("clip1.wav", "rb").read()
clone_from_samples("ada")  # uploads the samples, saves the profile

model = create_speech_model("elevenlabs")
model.generate_speech("Hi!", load_voice("ada"), output_path="hi.wav")
```

## Configuration

You can configure the default device by setting the `DFLT_VOXY_DEVICE` environment variable:

```bash
# Use CUDA
export DFLT_VOXY_DEVICE=cuda

# Use CPU
export DFLT_VOXY_DEVICE=cpu

# Use MPS (Apple Silicon)
export DFLT_VOXY_DEVICE=mps
```

## Advanced Usage

### Audio Cleanup

The module includes an audio cleanup function that normalizes volume and removes silence:

```python
from voxy import cleanup_audio
import torchaudio

# Load audio
audio, sample_rate = torchaudio.load("noisy_audio.wav")

# Clean up audio
cleaned_audio = cleanup_audio(
    audio=audio,
    sample_rate=sample_rate,
    normalize=True,
    remove_silence=True,
    silence_threshold=0.02,
    min_silence_duration=0.2,
)

# Save cleaned audio
torchaudio.save("cleaned_audio.wav", cleaned_audio, sample_rate)
```

### Disabling Audio Cleanup

You can disable audio cleanup when cloning a voice:

```python
voice_profile = model.clone_voice(
    audio_input="sample_voice.wav",
    transcript="This is a sample of my voice.",
    cleanup_audio_fn=None,  # Disable audio cleanup
)
```

### Custom Audio Cleanup

You can also provide your own audio cleanup function:

```python
def my_custom_cleanup(audio, sample_rate, **kwargs):
    # Custom cleanup logic
    return processed_audio

voice_profile = model.
```

# _autosummary/voxy.aix_model.html.md

# voxy.aix_model

Speech through aix (LiteLLM): OpenAI’s TTS voices and the other providers LiteLLM routes.

The provider is picked by the `model` string (e.g. `"gpt-4o-mini-tts"`,
`"tts-1-hd"`); keys and defaults come from aix’s own config. aix is imported
lazily (`pip install 'voxy[aix]'`).

```pycon
>>> AixSpeechModel(tts=lambda text, **kw: None).name
'aix'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`OPENAI_TTS_VOICES`](_autosummary/voxy.aix_model.html.md#voxy.aix_model.OPENAI_TTS_VOICES)   | OpenAI's built-in TTS voices (which ones a model accepts depends on the model).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`AixSpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.aix_model.html.md#voxy.aix_model.AixSpeechModel)(\*[, model, response_format, tts])   | aix/LiteLLM text-to-speech as a voxy backend.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|

### *class* voxy.aix_model.AixSpeechModel(, model=None, response_format='mp3', tts=None)

Bases: [`SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel)

aix/LiteLLM text-to-speech as a voxy backend.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – TTS model (None: aix’s configured default).
  * **response_format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – ‘mp3’, ‘opus’, ‘aac’, ‘flac’, ‘wav’…
  * **tts** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(text, **kw) -> GeneratedAudio` (tests inject a fake).

# _autosummary/voxy.base.html.md

# voxy.base

Voxy: A flexible speech synthesis and voice cloning module.

This module provides a plugin architecture for working with different speech synthesis
models, with initial support for the CSM-1B model.

torch, torchaudio and whisper are imported only where a local model needs them
(`voxy[local]`, `voxy[transcription]`), so a cloud backend runs without them.
Annotations are postponed and torch is imported only for type checking, so
`typing.get_type_hints` on these functions needs torch importable and in scope
(an accepted trade-off).

### Module Attributes

| [`OPTIONAL_MODULE_EXTRAS`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.OPTIONAL_MODULE_EXTRAS)   | The extra that installs each optional module (for the error raised without it).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`speech_model_factories`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.speech_model_factories)   | Backend name -> factory (keys lowercase).                                         |
| [`backend_aliases`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.backend_aliases)          | Other names for a backend -> its registry name (one model, one profile type).     |

### Functions

| [`audio_to_text`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.audio_to_text)(audio_input[, model_size, ...])   | Transcribe audio to text using Whisper.                                                  |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`canonical_backend`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.canonical_backend)(name)                         | The registry name of backend `name` (lowercased, aliases resolved).                      |
| [`cleanup_audio`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.cleanup_audio)(audio, sample_rate[, ...])        | Clean up audio by normalizing volume and removing silence.                               |
| [`create_speech_model`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.create_speech_model)([model_type])               | Create a speech model of the specified type.                                             |
| [`dflt_voxy_device`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.dflt_voxy_device)()                              | `$DFLT_VOXY_DEVICE`, else 'cuda' if torch is installed and sees one, else 'cpu'.         |
| [`is_tensor`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.is_tensor)(obj)                                  | True if `obj` is a torch tensor (without importing torch to find out).                   |
| [`optional_import`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.optional_import)(module)                         | Import `module`, or raise an ImportError naming the voxy extra that has it.              |

### voxy.base.cleanup_audio(audio, sample_rate, normalize=True, remove_silence=True, silence_threshold=0.02, min_silence_duration=0.2)

Clean up audio by normalizing volume and removing silence.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** (`Tensor`) – Audio tensor [channels, samples] or [samples]
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Sample rate of the audio
  * **normalize** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to normalize the audio volume
  * **remove_silence** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Whether to remove silence
  * **silence_threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Threshold for silence detection (0.0-1.0)
  * **min_silence_duration** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Minimum silence duration in seconds
* **Return type:**
  `Tensor`
* **Returns:**
  Processed audio tensor

A 1-D input is given a channel dimension, and the loudest sample is
normalized to 1.0:

```pycon
>>> import torch
>>> audio = torch.tensor([0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0])
>>> processed = cleanup_audio(audio, sample_rate=8000)
>>> tuple(processed.shape)
(1, 4)
>>> round(float(processed.max()), 3)
1.0
```

Stereo input is mixed down to mono:

```pycon
>>> stereo = torch.tensor([[0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0]])
>>> tuple(cleanup_audio(stereo, sample_rate=8000).shape)
(1, 4)
```

### voxy.base.create_speech_model(model_type='csm', \*\*kwargs)

Create a speech model of the specified type.

* **Parameters:**
  * **model_type** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A key of `speech_model_factories` (‘csm’, ‘csm-1b’,
    ‘elevenlabs’, ‘aix’, ‘fal’, ‘say’, ‘voicestudio’, or any registered); case-insensitive,
    aliases in `backend_aliases` accepted.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Additional model-specific parameters
* **Return type:**
  [`SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel)
* **Returns:**
  SpeechModel instance
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – If the model type is not supported

The returned model loads its (large) weights lazily, on first use:

```pycon
>>> model = create_speech_model("csm")
>>> type(model).__name__
'CSMSpeechModel'
>>> type(create_speech_model("elevenlabs", api_key="unused")).__name__
'ElevenLabsSpeechModel'
>>> create_speech_model("no-such-model")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: Unsupported model type: no-such-model (supported: csm, elevenlabs, ...)
```

### voxy.base.register_speech_model(name, factory, , overwrite=False)

Register a backend (a class or `**kwargs -> SpeechModel` callable).

Returns `factory`, so it also works as a class decorator via `functools.partial`.

```pycon
>>> class Echo(SpeechModel):
...     name = "echo"
>>> _ = register_speech_model("echo", Echo)
>>> type(create_speech_model("echo")).__name__
'Echo'
>>> register_speech_model("echo", Echo)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: A speech backend named 'echo' is already registered (pass overwrite=True)
>>> del speech_model_factories["echo"]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel)]

### voxy.base.speech_model_factories *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Callable](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[..., [SpeechModel](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel)]]* *= {'aix': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'chatterbox': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'csm': <class 'voxy.base.CSMSpeechModel'>, 'elevenlabs': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'f5tts': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'fal': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'kokoro': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'qwen3tts': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'say': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'voicestudio': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'voxcpm': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>, 'xtts': <function \_lazy_factory.<locals>.factory>}*

Backend name -> factory (keys lowercase). Add one with `register_speech_model`.

### voxy.base.tensor_to_wav_bytes(audio, sample_rate)

Encode audio ([samples], [channels, samples] or [samples, channels]) as mono
16-bit WAV.

`audio` is a numpy array or a torch tensor (torch is not needed for arrays).
Integer audio is taken as PCM and scaled to [-1, 1] first (8-bit PCM is
unsigned). A 2-D input is `[channels, samples]` unless it has more rows than
columns, which only `[samples, channels]` (soundfile’s layout) can have (a
square input is read channels-first); channels are averaged, and
`voxy.wavutil.write_wav` does the encoding.

```pycon
>>> data = tensor_to_wav_bytes(np.zeros(160), 16000)
>>> data[:4], len(data)
(b'RIFF', 364)
>>> tensor_to_wav_bytes(np.array([[0, 32767]], dtype=np.int16), 8000)[-2:]
b'\xff\x7f'
>>> tensor_to_wav_bytes(np.full((5, 2), 128, dtype=np.uint8), 8000)[-4:]  # silence
b'\x00\x00\x00\x00'
>>> tensor_to_wav_bytes(np.zeros((1, 2, 3)), 8000)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ValueError: Audio must be 1-D or 2-D (channels and samples), not 3-D
```

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)


# _autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md

# voxy.benchmarks

Published benchmarks of the cloning backends, kept as data, rendered as tables and charts.

The data (`voxy/data/benchmarks.json`) has two parts: `models` (licence, size, languages,
price, watermark per backend id such as `"qwen3tts"` or `"elevenlabs/eleven_v3"`) and
`results`, one row per published number:

```default
{model, benchmark, metric, value, higher_is_better, source_url, self_reported, retrieved, note?}
```

`docs/benchmarks.md` holds the prose; its tables and charts are generated between markers
(`<!-- voxy-benchmarks:NAME -->` … `<!-- /voxy-benchmarks -->`) by `render_docs`, from the
`TABLES` and `CHARTS` specs below. To update: edit the JSON (add rows, keep every source URL),
then `python -m voxy benchmarks docs/benchmarks.md`.

```pycon
>>> rows = [{"model": "a", "benchmark": "B", "metric": "WER %", "value": 2.0, "self_reported": True,
...          "source_url": "https://x.org/p"}]
>>> print(results_table(rows, [("B", "WER %")], models={"a": {"name": "Model A"}}))
| Model | B (WER %) |
|---|---|
| Model A | [2.0](https://x.org/p) (S) |
```

### Functions

| [`chart`](_autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md#voxy.benchmarks.chart)(rows, spec, path, \*[, models])             | Draw one `CHARTS` spec to an image file (SVG or PNG by extension; needs matplotlib).    |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`facts_table`](_autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md#voxy.benchmarks.facts_table)(models, \*[, columns])                | A Markdown table of each backend's practical facts (licence, French, price, ...).       |
| [`load_benchmarks`](_autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md#voxy.benchmarks.load_benchmarks)([path])                           | The benchmark data: `{"retrieved", "models", "results"}` (default: the shipped file).   |
| [`render_docs`](_autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md#voxy.benchmarks.render_docs)(doc_path, \*[, data, tables, ...])    | Regenerate the generated blocks of a benchmarks doc; return the names updated.          |
| [`results_table`](_autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md#voxy.benchmarks.results_table)(rows, columns, \*[, models])        | A Markdown table: one row per model with any value, one column per (benchmark, metric). |
| [`select`](_autosummary/voxy.benchmarks.html.md#voxy.benchmarks.select)(rows, \*[, benchmark, metric, model, ...]) | The rows matching every filter given (`source`: a substring of `source_url`).           |

### voxy.benchmarks.render_docs(doc_path, , data=None, tables={'french': [('CV3-eval: French', 'WER %'), ('CV3-eval: French', 'SIM (cosine, 0-1)'), ('MiniMax multilingual test: French', 'WER %'), ('MiniMax multilingual test: French', 'SIM (cosine, 0-1)')], 'human': [('Hume Voice Replication Leaderboard (overall, 13 models)', 'same-speaker rating (1-5)'), ('Hume Voice Replication Leaderboard (overall, 13 models)', 'different-person %'), ('Artificial Analysis Controlled Voice arena (8 cloned EN voices, 44 models)', 'Elo'), ('TTS Arena V2 (TTS-AGI, 39 listed)', 'Elo')], 'seed': [('Seed-TTS-eval test-en', 'WER %'), ('Seed-TTS-eval test-en', 'SIM (cosine, 0-1)'), ('Seed-TTS-eval test-zh', 'CER %'), ('Seed-TTS-eval test-zh', 'SIM (cosine, 0-1)')]}, charts={'cloned-voice-arena': {'kind': 'bar', 'title': 'Blind preference votes on cloned voices (Artificial Analysis, Elo)', 'y': ('Artificial Analysis Controlled Voice arena (8 cloned EN voices, 44 models)', 'Elo')}, 'french-tradeoff': {'kind': 'scatter', 'source': 'open_tts_leaderboard', 'title': 'French cloning: intelligibility vs likeness (CV3-eval, HF Open TTS Leaderboard)', 'x': ('CV3-eval: French', 'WER %'), 'y': ('CV3-eval: French', 'SIM (cosine, 0-1)')}, 'human-likeness': {'kind': 'bar', 'title': 'Human raters: does it sound like the reference person? (Hume, 1-5)', 'y': ('Hume Voice Replication Leaderboard (overall, 13 models)', 'same-speaker rating (1-5)')}}, charts_dir='benchmarks', draw=True)

Regenerate the generated blocks of a benchmarks doc; return the names updated.

A block `<!-- voxy-benchmarks:NAME -->...<!-- /voxy-benchmarks -->` gets the table `NAME`
(`facts` is the practical-facts table), or the chart `NAME` drawn to
`<charts_dir>/NAME.svg` next to the doc and embedded as an image.

* **Return type:**

# _autosummary/voxy.diagnosis.html.md

# voxy.diagnosis

Diagnosis pages: render one text through a grid of (model x parameters), listen side by side.

```pycon
>>> from voxy import diagnosis
>>> variants = diagnosis.expand_grid([
...     {"backend": "f5tts", "params": {"nfe_step": [16, 32], "cfg_strength": 2}},
...     {"backend": "chatterbox", "params": {"exaggeration": [0.3, 0.6]}},
... ])
>>> results = diagnosis.render_grid(text, references, variants, "out/")
>>> diagnosis.build_page(results, "out/", title="First listen")
```

Or from a spec file: `python -m voxy diagnose spec.json --out DIR --publish`.

Every variant has a stable ID (`F5-7KQ2`) computed from its backend, model
options, parameters and reference clip, never from the text, so “use F5-7KQ2”
means the same configuration on every page and every chapter. The page shows,
per variant, the ID, an audio player, the parameters (those that differ from the
model’s defaults in bold), generation time and real-time factor, and lets each
listener rate it (1-5) and write a note. Ratings stay in the listener’s browser;
“Copy my notes” turns them into a text block to paste into a message.

For a page shared with other listeners: `notes_sink` saves every rating and
note as it is made (to an annoquest server, whose owner page then lists them per
listener), `appendix` folds the variants of some references into a collapsed
section, and `imported` adds clips rendered elsewhere (a cloud service).

### Module Attributes

| [`BACKEND_NAMES`](_autosummary/voxy.diagnosis.html.md#voxy.diagnosis.BACKEND_NAMES)      | Display names for page sections and default variant labels.                 |

    the local backend’s notes and licence).

### voxy.diagnosis.expand_grid(grid, , references=('',))

Variants from grid rows: list values are swept (cartesian product), scalars fixed.

A row: `{"backend": ..., "params": {...}, "init": {...}, "label": ...}`.
`init` values may be lists too (e.g. `{"variant": ["original", "turbo"]}`).
Every variant is rendered once per reference name, except a stock-voice backend’s
(kokoro): its rows are not crossed with references; sweep its voices with
`params={"voice": [...]}`.

```pycon
>>> vs = expand_grid([{"backend": "f5tts", "params": {"nfe_step": [16, 32], "speed": 1}}])
>>> [(v.backend, v.params) for v in vs]
[('f5tts', {'nfe_step': 16, 'speed': 1}), ('f5tts', {'nfe_step': 32, 'speed': 1})]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Variant`](_autosummary/voxy.diagnosis.html.md#voxy.diagnosis.Variant)]

Each entry: `backend`, `audio_file`, and optionally `params`, `init`,

* **Return type:**

`(voices, shown)`: reference voices for rendering, and their page entries.

The spec names references directly (`"references": {name: {ref_audio, ref_text}}`)

  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.diagnosis.render_grid(text, references, variants, out_dir, \*, model_factory=None, audio_format='mp3', resume=True, log=<built-in function print>)

Render every variant to `out_dir/audio/<id>.<format>`; return (and save) the results.

Models are built one backend configuration at a time and closed before the
next, so only one model is in memory. With `resume`, variants already in
`results.json` (without error) are not rendered again.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What every variant says.
  * **references** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)) – Reference name -> voice (a `VoiceProfile` or `{"ref_audio", "ref_text"}`).
  * **variants** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Variant`](_autosummary/voxy.diagnosis.html.md#voxy.diagnosis.Variant)]) – From `expand_grid` (their `reference` names key `references`).
  * **model_factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(backend, **init) -> SpeechModel` (default `create_speech_model`).
  * **audio_format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – ‘mp3’ (default, small) or ‘wav’.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.diagnosis.run_spec(spec, out_dir, \*, log=<built-in function print>)

Render a spec’s grid and build its page; return the page path.

Spec keys: `title`, `text` (or `text_file`), `references` or `voice`
(+ `n_references`), `grid` (rows for `expand_grid`), optional `intro`,
`audio_format`, `imported` (see `import_results`), `appendix`,
`backend_notes`, `noindex` and `notes_sink` (see `build_page`). With an
annoquest `notes_sink` and a `page_url` (where the page will be served), the
request to register on that server is written next to the page.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### voxy.diagnosis.variant_labels(results)

Readable names: the backend’s name, then the values of the settings that vary
between that backend’s variants. A result’s own `label` wins.

```pycon
>>> rs = [
...     {"id": "a", "backend": "chatterbox", "params": {"language": "fr", "exaggeration": 0.3}},
...     {"id": "b", "backend": "chatterbox", "params": {"language": "fr", "exaggeration": 0.5}},
...     {"id": "c", "backend": "voxcpm", "params": {"cfg_value": 2.0}},
...     {"id": "d", "backend": "elevenlabs", "label": "ElevenLabs v3"},
... ]
>>> variant_labels(rs)

```

# _autosummary/voxy.elevenlabs_model.html.md

# voxy.elevenlabs_model

ElevenLabs backend for voxy: instant voice cloning and synthesis through the API.

Select it with `create_speech_model("elevenlabs")`. Cloning uploads one or more
audio samples to ElevenLabs’ Instant Voice Cloning (IVC) endpoint and returns a
`VoiceProfile` whose `segment` is the new `voice_id`; synthesis renders text
in that voice. ElevenLabs keeps the voice, so a later session can rebuild the
profile from the id alone with `ElevenLabsSpeechModel.voice_profile(voice_id)`.

The key is read from `api_key=` or, failing that, the `ELEVEN_API_KEY` /
`ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` environment variables (the same order the fleet’s other
ElevenLabs clients use). The `elevenlabs` SDK is imported lazily, so it is only
needed when a request is actually made (`pip install voxy[elevenlabs]`).

ElevenLabs requires that whoever clones a voice has the right and the consent of
the voice’s owner (or their guardian) to do so.

```pycon
>>> model = ElevenLabsSpeechModel(api_key="unused", client_factory=lambda key: None)
>>> model.sample_rate
24000
```

### Functions

| [`default_elevenlabs_client_factory`](_autosummary/voxy.elevenlabs_model.html.md#voxy.elevenlabs_model.default_elevenlabs_client_factory)(api_key)     | Build the official SDK client (imported lazily).                        |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`resolve_elevenlabs_api_key`](_autosummary/voxy.elevenlabs_model.html.md#voxy.elevenlabs_model.resolve_elevenlabs_api_key)([api_key, envvars]) | The explicit `api_key` if given, else the first set env var, else None. |

### Classes

| [`ElevenLabsSpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.elevenlabs_model.html.md#voxy.elevenlabs_model.ElevenLabsSpeechModel)(\*[, api_key, ...])     | Speech model backed by the ElevenLabs API (Instant Voice Cloning + TTS).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`VoiceDesignPreview`](_autosummary/voxy.elevenlabs_model.html.md#voxy.elevenlabs_model.VoiceDesignPreview)(generated_voice_id, audio) | One candidate voice from `design_voice_previews`: listen, then pick.       |

Speech model backed by the ElevenLabs API (Instant Voice Cloning + TTS).

  * **model_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – TTS model used by `generate_speech`.

Defaults to the official SDK; tests

#### *property* client

#### clone_voice(audio_input, transcript=None, speaker_id=999, , cleanup_audio_fn=None, name=None, description=None, labels=None, remove_background_noise=None, assumed_sample_rate=16000, max_files=25)

Create an ElevenLabs instant voice clone from one or more audio samples.

ElevenLabs recommends about 1-2 minutes of clean, single-speaker audio in
total (at least 1, at most about 3); how it is split across files does
not matter.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio_input** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike), [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes), [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO), `Tensor`, `ndarray`, [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike), [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes), [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO), `Tensor`, `ndarray`]], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike), [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes), [`BinaryIO`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.BinaryIO), `Tensor`, `ndarray`], [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]]) – One audio input, or an iterable of them (paths, bytes,
    file-likes, tensors, arrays).
  * **transcript** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Ignored: IVC needs no transcript. Kept so every voxy
    backend shares one `clone_voice` signature.
  * **speaker_id** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Carried on the profile, and used in the default name.
  * **cleanup_audio_fn** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Optional `(audio, sample_rate) -> audio` applied
    before upload. Off by default: ElevenLabs does its own processing,
    and voxy’s silence trimmer can chop soft speech.
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice name shown in ElevenLabs (default `voxy-<speaker_id>`).
  * **description** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice description.
  * **labels** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice labels (keys such as language, accent, gender, age).
  * **remove_background_noise** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Ask ElevenLabs to isolate the voice. Can
    make clean samples worse.
  * **assumed_sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Sample rate of raw tensor/array inputs.
  * **max_files** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Refuse, before uploading anything, more samples than
    ElevenLabs accepts per voice (`None` to skip the check).
    Concatenate short clips to stay under it.
* **Return type:**
  [`VoiceProfile`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.VoiceProfile)
* **Returns:**
  A `VoiceProfile` whose `segment` (and `metadata['voice_id']`)
  is the new ElevenLabs voice id.

#### design_voice(description, , preview=None, name=None, labels=None, speaker_id=999, \*\*preview_kwargs)

  * **preview** ([`VoiceDesignPreview`](_autosummary/voxy.elevenlabs_model.html.md#voxy.elevenlabs_model.VoiceDesignPreview) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The chosen preview (or its `generated_voice_id`) from

    and the first is used.

  * **labels** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice labels (language, accent, gender, age…).
  * **\*\*preview_kwargs** – Passed to `design_voice_previews` when
    `preview` is omitted.
* **Return type:**
  [`VoiceProfile`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.VoiceProfile)

#### design_voice_previews(description, , text=None, model_id='eleven_multilingual_ttv_v2', seed=None, guidance_scale=None, loudness=None, \*\*design_kwargs)

Candidate voices for a text `description` (ElevenLabs Voice Design).

`text` (100-1000 characters) is what the previews say; without it
ElevenLabs writes a fitting line. Nothing is added to the account until
one preview is passed to `design_voice`.

  * **voice_profile** ([`VoiceProfile`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.VoiceProfile) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – From `clone_voice` or `voice_profile`, or a bare

  * **output_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – If given, save the audio there (WAV for pcm/wav formats,
    the raw payload otherwise).
  * **max_length_ms** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Ignored; ElevenLabs sizes the audio to the text.
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Passed to `synthesize_bytes`.
* **Return type:**

Voices in the account and its library (`voice_type`: e.g. ‘default’,

# _autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md

# voxy.envs

Isolated Python environments for backends whose dependencies clash with yours.

Local voice-cloning models each pin their own torch, transformers and numpy, so
they can’t share one environment (or yours). A backend declares an `EnvSpec`;
`ensure_env` builds it once with `uv` under the data root and returns its
interpreter, which `voxy.worker` then runs the model in:

> envs/{name}/            one virtual environment per backend
> models/hf/              model weights (`HF_HOME` of every worker)
> models/{name}/          a backend’s other weights (e.g. Coqui’s `TTS_HOME`)

Nothing here is downloaded at import time; building an environment is explicit
(`ensure_env`, or `python -m voxy setup <backend>`).

```pycon
>>> spec = EnvSpec("demo", ("numpy",))
>>> spec.digest() == EnvSpec("demo", ("numpy",)).digest()
True
>>> env_dir(spec, rootdir="/data").as_posix()
'/data/envs/demo'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_NUM_THREADS`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.DFLT_NUM_THREADS)   | a shared machine keeps headroom for others.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`ensure_env`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.ensure_env)(spec, \*[, rootdir, run, log])          | Build `spec`'s environment if missing or stale, and return its interpreter.      |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`env_dir`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.env_dir)(spec, \*[, rootdir])                       | The folder of `spec`'s environment (not created here).                           |
| [`env_python`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.env_python)(spec, \*[, rootdir])                    | The interpreter of `spec`'s environment (it may not exist yet).                  |
| [`is_env_ready`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.is_env_ready)(spec, \*[, rootdir])                  | True if the environment exists and was built from this exact spec.               |
| [`models_dir`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.models_dir)(\*parts[, rootdir])                     | Where weights live (`models/`, or a subfolder of it).                            |
| [`num_threads`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.num_threads)([threads])                             | `threads`, else `$VOXY_NUM_THREADS`, else `DFLT_NUM_THREADS`.                    |
| [`remove_env`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.remove_env)(spec, \*[, rootdir])                    | Delete `spec`'s environment (weights are kept).                                  |
| [`worker_environ`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.worker_environ)(spec, \*[, threads, rootdir, base]) | Environment variables for a worker: weights under the data root, threads capped. |

### Classes

| [`EnvSpec`](_autosummary/voxy.envs.html.md#voxy.envs.EnvSpec)(name, requirements[, python, ...])   | What a backend's environment holds.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|

### voxy.envs.DFLT_NUM_THREADS *= 8*

a shared machine keeps headroom for others.

* **Type:**
  Torch/ONNX threads per worker

### *class* voxy.envs.EnvSpec(name, requirements, python='3.11', torch_backend='cpu', env_vars=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a backend’s environment holds.

* **Parameters:**
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Folder name under `envs/` (usually the backend name).
  * **requirements** ([`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)]) – `uv pip install` arguments (packages, pins, extras).
  * **python** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Python version for `uv venv`.
  * **torch_backend** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `uv`’s `--torch-backend` (‘cpu’ keeps CUDA wheels out;
    None leaves the index alone).
  * **env_vars** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Extra environment variables for the worker process (values may
    use `{models}`, the backend’s own weights folder).

#### digest()

A short hash of what is installed (env vars excluded: they don’t need a rebuild).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

The interpreter of `spec`’s environment (it may not exist yet).

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

True if the environment exists and was built from this exact spec.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### voxy.envs.models_dir(\*parts, rootdir=None)

### voxy.envs.num_threads(threads=None)

`threads`, else `$VOXY_NUM_THREADS`, else `DFLT_NUM_THREADS`.

```pycon
>>> num_threads(4)

```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

Environment variables for a worker: weights under the data root, threads capped.

```pycon
>>> env = worker_environ(EnvSpec("x", (), env_vars={"TTS_HOME": "{models}"}),
...                      threads=2, rootdir="/d", base={})
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> env["OMP_NUM_THREADS"], Path(env["HF_HOME"]).as_posix(), Path(env["TTS_HOME"]).as_posix()

```

# _autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md

# voxy.facade

Voice generation in one call, whatever the service behind it.

```pycon
>>> import voxy
>>> voxy.text_to_speech("Hello!", voice="ada").save("hi.mp3")
>>> voxy.text_to_speech("Hello!", voice="Daniel", backend="say")
>>> voxy.list_voices()               # the library: our named voices
>>> voxy.list_voices("elevenlabs")   # a backend's own voices
>>> voxy.voice_id("addie")            # 'xY12...' (aliases work)
```

How `voice` is understood, first match wins:

1. a `VoiceProfile`: used as is, on its own backend;
2. a name or alias in the voice library (`voxy.voices_store()`): that voice’s
   saved profile for `backend` (or, if `backend` is not given, its first one);
3. anything else: the backend’s own voice id or name (e.g. ‘nova’, ‘Daniel’);
4. `None`: the backend’s default voice, if it has one.

Pass `use_library=False` to reach a backend voice whose name is also a library
name or alias. With no `backend`, a library voice uses its profile for the
default backend if it has one, else its `default_backend`, else its first.

Backends are entries of `voxy.speech_model_factories`; add one with
`voxy.register_speech_model`. The default backend is `$VOXY_TTS_BACKEND`
(read at call time), else ‘elevenlabs’.

### Functions

| [`clear_speech_models`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.clear_speech_models)([models])                    | Forget cached models (e.g. after changing keys or settings).                    |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dflt_tts_backend`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.dflt_tts_backend)()                               | `$VOXY_TTS_BACKEND`, else 'elevenlabs' (read on every call).                    |
| [`get_speech_model`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.get_speech_model)([backend, models])              | The (cached) model for `backend`; `models` replaces the shared cache.           |
| [`list_voices`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.list_voices)([backend, voices, model, models])    | Our named voices (`backend=None`), or the voices a backend offers.              |
| [`resolve_voice`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.resolve_voice)(voice, \*[, backend, voices, ...]) | `(backend, voice)` to synthesize with (see the module docstring for the rules). |
| [`speech_to_speech`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.speech_to_speech)(audio[, voice, backend, ...])   | Voice changer: re-speak `audio` in `voice`, keeping its timing and intonation.  |
| [`text_to_speech`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.text_to_speech)(text[, voice, backend, ...])      | Speak `text` in `voice` and return the encoded audio (`.save(path)`).           |
| [`voice_id`](_autosummary/voxy.facade.html.md#voxy.facade.voice_id)(name, \*[, backend, voices])            | The provider's id for library voice `name` (for code that calls a provider).    |

### voxy.facade.clear_speech_models(models=None)

Forget cached models (e.g. after changing keys or settings).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.facade.dflt_tts_backend()

`$VOXY_TTS_BACKEND`, else ‘elevenlabs’ (read on every call).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.facade.get_speech_model(backend=None, , models=None)

The (cached) model for `backend`; `models` replaces the shared cache.

* **Return type:**
  [`SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel)

### voxy.facade.list_voices(backend=None, , voices=None, model=None, models=None, \*\*kwargs)

Our named voices (`backend=None`), or the voices a backend offers.

```pycon
>>> lib = {"ada": {"name": "ada", "aliases": ["Addie"], "description": "d",
...                 "profiles": {"elevenlabs": {"segment": "v1"}}}}
>>> [(v.name, v.labels["backends"]) for v in list_voices(voices=lib)]
[('ada', ['elevenlabs'])]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`VoiceInfo`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.VoiceInfo)]

### voxy.facade.resolve_voice(voice, , backend=None, voices=None, use_library=True)

`(backend, voice)` to synthesize with (see the module docstring for the rules).

```pycon
>>> lib = {"ada": {"name": "ada", "aliases": ["Addie"], "profiles": {
...     "elevenlabs": {"segment": "v1", "speaker_id": 1, "model_type": "elevenlabs",
...                    "sample_rate": 24000}}}}
>>> b, v = resolve_voice("addie", voices=lib)
>>> b, v.segment
('elevenlabs', 'v1')
>>> resolve_voice("Daniel", backend="say", voices=lib)
('say', 'Daniel')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`VoiceProfile`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.VoiceProfile) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### voxy.facade.speech_to_speech(audio, voice=None, , backend='elevenlabs', output_path=None, voices=None, model=None, models=None, use_library=True, \*\*kwargs)

Voice changer: re-speak `audio` in `voice`, keeping its timing and intonation.

Same voice resolution as `text_to_speech`. Needs a backend with a
`speech_to_speech` method (ElevenLabs). `audio` is a path, bytes, file-like
or tensor. Use it to correct a word: say the fix yourself, convert it to the
narrator’s voice, splice.

* **Return type:**
  [`Speech`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.Speech)

### voxy.facade.text_to_speech(text, voice=None, , backend=None, output_path=None, voices=None, model=None, models=None, use_library=True, \*\*kwargs)

Speak `text` in `voice` and return the encoded audio (`.save(path)`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What to say.
  * **voice** ([`VoiceProfile`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.VoiceProfile) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A library name or alias (‘ada’, ‘Addie’), a backend’s own voice
    (‘nova’, ‘Daniel’, an ElevenLabs id), a `VoiceProfile`, or None.
  * **backend** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Service to use (‘elevenlabs’, ‘say’, ‘aix’, ‘fal’, ‘csm’, or
    any registered). Inferred from library voices.
  * **output_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Also save the audio there.
  * **voices** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice library store (default `voxy.voices_store()`).
  * **model** ([`SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A ready model to use (its backend is then the backend).
  * **models** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Model cache to use instead of the shared one.
  * **use_library** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Look `voice` up in the library first (False: always
    the backend’s own voice of that name).
  * **\*\*kwargs** – Backend-specific options (e.g. `output_format=` for
    ElevenLabs, `speed=` for aix, `quality=` for fal).
* **Return type:**
  [`Speech`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.Speech)

### voxy.facade.voice_id(name, , backend='elevenlabs', voices=None)

The provider’s id for library voice `name` (for code that calls a provider).

```pycon
>>> lib = {"ada": {"name": "ada", "aliases": ["Addie"], "profiles": {
...     "elevenlabs": {"segment": "v1", "speaker_id": 1, "model_type": "elevenlabs",
...                    "sample_rate": 24000}}}}
>>> voice_id("Addie", voices=lib)
'v1'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/voxy.fal_model.html.md

# voxy.fal_model

Speech through fal.ai, via falaw: many hosted TTS models, chosen by quality tier.

falaw picks a model for `quality` (‘fast’, ‘balanced’, ‘best’…) unless
`model_id` is given; `voice` means whatever that model calls a voice. falaw is
imported lazily (`pip install 'voxy[fal]'`).

```pycon
>>> FalSpeechModel(tts=lambda text, **kw: None, fetch=lambda url: b"").name
'fal'
```

### Classes

| [`FalSpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.fal_model.html.md#voxy.fal_model.FalSpeechModel)(\*[, quality, model_id, tts, ...])   | fal.ai text-to-speech (through falaw) as a voxy backend.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|

Bases: [`SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel)

fal.ai text-to-speech (through falaw) as a voxy backend.

* **Parameters:**

  * **model_id** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A specific fal model (overrides `quality`).
  * **tts** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(text, **kw) -> falaw.Result` (tests inject a fake).
  * **fetch** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `url -> bytes` to download the result.

#### name *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= 'fal'*

# _autosummary/voxy.finetune.html.md

# voxy.finetune

Fine-tuning datasets from prepared clips: one export per training recipe.

`voxy.refprep.prepare_reference` leaves scored, transcribed clips and a
manifest; `export_dataset` writes the subset worth training on in the layout a
recipe expects:

- `ljspeech`: `wavs/{id}.wav` + `metadata.csv` (`id|text|text`, no header).
  Read by Coqui’s XTTS-v2 GPT fine-tuning (formatter `ljspeech`), StyleTTS2 and
  most community recipes (Chatterbox fine-tuning included).
- `f5tts`: `wavs/` + `metadata.csv` with an `audio_file|text` header and
  absolute paths, the input of `f5-tts_prepare_csv_wavs` then `f5-tts_finetune-cli`.

Plus `train.txt` / `eval.txt` (a deterministic split) for recipes that want one.
Commands to run each recipe on a rented GPU are in `finetune_commands`.

```pycon
>>> rows = [{"key": "clips/a.wav", "text": "Hi there.", "score": 0.9, "duration": 4.0},
...         {"key": "clips/b.wav", "text": "Noisy.", "score": 0.2, "duration": 3.0}]
>>> [r["key"] for r in select_clips(rows, min_score=0.5)]
['clips/a.wav']
```

### Functions

| [`export_dataset`](_autosummary/voxy.finetune.html.md#voxy.finetune.export_dataset)(manifest, samples, out_dir, \*)     | Write the training set to `out_dir` and return a summary.                        |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`finetune_commands`](_autosummary/voxy.finetune.html.md#voxy.finetune.finetune_commands)(backend, dataset_dir, \*[, ...]) | Shell commands to fine-tune `backend` on an exported dataset (run on a GPU box). |
| [`select_clips`](_autosummary/voxy.finetune.html.md#voxy.finetune.select_clips)(manifest, \*[, min_score, ...])       | Clips good enough to train on (score and length within bounds, some text).       |

### voxy.finetune.export_dataset(manifest, samples, out_dir, , format='ljspeech', min_score=0.5, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=15.0, eval_fraction=0.05, latest_only=True)

Write the training set to `out_dir` and return a summary.

* **Parameters:**
  * **manifest** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]) – From `prepare_reference` (or `refprep.load_manifest`).
  * **samples** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)) – The store the clips are in (`key -> wav bytes`).
  * **format** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – One of `FORMATS`.
  * **latest_only** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Train on each source’s latest run only (see `select_clips`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.finetune.finetune_commands(backend, dataset_dir, , name='voice')

Shell commands to fine-tune `backend` on an exported dataset (run on a GPU box).

```pycon
>>> "f5-tts_finetune-cli" in finetune_commands("f5tts", "/data/ds")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.finetune.select_clips(manifest, , min_score=0.5, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=15.0, latest_only=True)

Clips good enough to train on (score and length within bounds, some text).

Entries without a numeric `score` or `duration`, a string `key` or `text`
(hand-added, or from an older voxy) are skipped. With `latest_only` (the default)
it picks from `refprep.latest_runs(manifest)`, so a source processed twice is
trained on once.

```pycon
>>> select_clips([{"key": "tape1.wav", "text": "x"}, {"score": 0.9}])
[]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

# _autosummary/voxy.kokoro_model.html.md

# voxy.kokoro_model

Kokoro: a neutral local voice that needs no reference clip, no key and no GPU.

Kokoro-82M (weights Apache-2.0) through `kokoro-onnx` (MIT) speaks in 54 stock
voices (`af_heart`, `am_michael`, `bf_emma`, …) and runs faster than
realtime on a CPU. It runs in its own small environment, like the local cloners
(`voxy.local_clone`): `python -m voxy setup kokoro` builds it, and the model
files (about 354 MB) are fetched from the Hugging Face hub on first use into
`$VOXY_DATA_DIR/models/hf`, like every other local backend’s weights.

```pycon
>>> import voxy
>>> voxy.text_to_speech("Hello.", "bf_emma", backend="kokoro").save("hi.wav")
```

A voice’s first letter is its language (`a` American English, `b` British,
`f` French, …) and its second its gender; `lang` follows the voice unless
you pass one. The voice list is static (`KOKORO_VOICES`), so listing voices
needs no model.

On macOS the espeak-ng bundled with kokoro-onnx (espeakng-loader) has its data
folder compiled in and cannot find it, so the first synthesis fails; use `say`
there (thorwhalen/voxy#61).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> fake = lambda text, **kw: (np.full(800, 0.1, dtype=np.float32), 24000)
>>> speech = KokoroSpeechModel(generate=fake).synthesize("One. Two.", "bm_george")
>>> speech.backend, speech.voice, speech.sample_rate
('kokoro', 'bm_george', 24000)
```

| [`KOKORO_VOICES`](_autosummary/voxy.kokoro_model.html.md#voxy.kokoro_model.KOKORO_VOICES)    | The voices in `voices-v1.0.bin`.                                       |

| [`KOKORO_GENDERS`](_autosummary/voxy.kokoro_model.html.md#voxy.kokoro_model.KOKORO_GENDERS)   | A voice name's second letter -> the voice's gender.                    |

### Functions

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`voice_info`](_autosummary/voxy.kokoro_model.html.md#voxy.kokoro_model.voice_info)(voice)    | What a stock voice's name says about it.                                    |

# _autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md

# voxy.lexique

French heteronyms derived from Lexique, to merge under voxy’s hand-made table.

Lexique (New, Pallier et al., [http://www.lexique.org](http://www.lexique.org)) lists about 140 000 French
word forms with their pronunciation, lemma, part of speech and frequency. Its
homographs that are not homophones (*est* /ɛ/ or /ɛst/, *couvent* /kuv/ or /kuvɑ̃/,
*président*…) are words a speech model can misread. voxy ships a short hand-made
table (`voxy.pronounce.heteronym_readings`) and no Lexique data, so derive more
from your own copy and let the hand-made readings win:

```pycon
>>> from voxy.lexique import lexique_heteronyms
>>> from voxy.pronounce import heteronym_readings
>>> derived = lexique_heteronyms("Lexique383.tsv", min_frequency=1)
>>> table = {**derived, **heteronym_readings("fr")}
>>> derived["couvent"]
{'noun': 'kuvɑ̃', 'verb': 'kuv'}
```

The derived table is not complete. Lexique stores one pronunciation per spelling,
part of speech and lemma, and no liaison or variant readings, so heteronyms that
differ only there are missing from it: *tous*, *os*, *six*, *dix*, *christ*,
*lacs*, *fait*. It extends the hand-made table; it does not replace it.

The result has the shape `voxy.pronounce` takes (`{word: {reading name: IPA}}`,
IPA in the symbols of its phoneme model). Pronunciations that differ only by
Lexique’s transcription noise are one reading and its variants (`verb~e`); a
reading is named by its part of speech, with the names of
`voxy.speechtext.FRENCH_READING_NAMES`, or by its lemma when two readings share a
part of speech:

```pycon
>>> rows = [
...     {"ortho": "est", "phon": "E", "lemme": "être", "cgram": "AUX", "freqfilms2": "100", "freqlivres": "90"},
...     {"ortho": "est", "phon": "e", "lemme": "être", "cgram": "VER", "freqfilms2": "9", "freqlivres": "9"},
...     {"ortho": "est", "phon": "Est", "lemme": "est", "cgram": "NOM", "freqfilms2": "20", "freqlivres": "30"},
...     {"ortho": "chat", "phon": "Sa", "lemme": "chat", "cgram": "NOM", "freqfilms2": "40", "freqlivres": "30"},
... ]
>>> heteronyms_from_rows(rows)
{'est': {'verb': 'ɛ', 'verb~e': 'e', 'noun': 'ɛst'}}
```

### Module Attributes

| [`LEXIQUE_TO_IPA`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.LEXIQUE_TO_IPA)             | Lexique's phonetic code -> IPA in the vocabulary of voxy's phoneme model (`facebook/wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft`); Lexique's other letters are that IPA.                                                                                             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TRANSCRIPTION_NOISE`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.TRANSCRIPTION_NOISE)        | two pronunciations equal after this are one reading (open/closed vowels, schwa).                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`LEXIQUE_TO_UPOS`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.LEXIQUE_TO_UPOS)            | Lexique's part of speech (`cgram`, whole or before its `:`) -> universal POS.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [`LEXIQUE_POS_NAMES`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.LEXIQUE_POS_NAMES)          | Lexique's part of speech -> a reading name (`voxy.speechtext.FRENCH_READING_NAMES`).                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`VERB_NAME`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.VERB_NAME)                  | A pronunciation with a verb row is named `verb` when its heaviest part of speech is one of these: Lexique tags some verb forms as nouns or adjectives too (*violent*, *insolent*), while an adverb (*plus*) is genuinely heavier than its verb rows. |
| [`UNTAGGED_NAME`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.UNTAGGED_NAME)              | The name of a reading whose part of speech Lexique leaves empty.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [`ORTHO`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.ORTHO)                      | Columns read from a Lexique 3 file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

| [`LEMMA`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.LEMMA)                      | Columns read from a Lexique 3 file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`CGRAM`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.CGRAM)                      | Columns read from a Lexique 3 file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`LEXIQUE_CACHE_KIND`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.LEXIQUE_CACHE_KIND)         | Folder (under voxy's cache) of derived tables, one JSON file per file and arguments.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`CACHE_KEY_CHARS`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.CACHE_KEY_CHARS)            | no collision among a user's tables).                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [`LEXIQUE_DERIVATION_VERSION`](_autosummary/voxy.lexique.html.md#voxy.lexique.LEXIQUE_DERIVATION_VERSION) | Bump when the derivation's rules change, so cached tables are derived afresh.                                                                                                                                                                        |
