### voxy.pronounce.align_words(text, words, , elisions=())

`{index of a word of text: index of the ASR word heard for it}`.

Words are matched by aligning the two sequences (`difflib`), so a word ASR missed,
merged or added elsewhere does not shift the others; a text word with no exact
counterpart is left out. A word elided onto one of `elisions` counts as two
(`_text_words()`).

```pycon
>>> align_words("Il est là", [{"text": " Il"}, {"text": " et"}, {"text": " est"}, {"text": " là."}])
{0: 0, 1: 2, 2: 3}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.pronounce.audit(text, audio, \*, readings=None, language='fr', elisions=None, clitics=None, expected=None, detectors=(), emitter=None, words_of=<function \_transcribed_words>, scoring='phrase', phonemize=None, context=1, filler_penalty=1.0, padding=0.08, margin=None, scorer=None)

Which reading did each heteronym of `text` get in the finished `audio`?

ASR (WER) checks cannot answer this: Whisper writes “est” whether the model said
/ɛ/ or /ɛst/. This flags the words of `text` that have several readings
([`voxy.speechtext.flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks)), finds each in the audio (ASR word times; the
n-th time the text has a word is the n-th time ASR heard it) and scores its
readings with the phoneme recogniser.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What the model was given (the speech text, not the display text).
  * **audio** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The render.
  * **readings** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `{word: {reading name: IPA}}`; default [`heteronym_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.heteronym_readings)
    for `language`.
  * **elisions** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `{clitic: IPA}` of the language’s elisions (default
    `ELISIONS[language]`): text and ASR words are split there to be aligned.
  * **clitics** ([`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The clitics a heteronym is still flagged after (default
    `NOUN_CLITICS[language]`): “l’Est” is the risk `Est`, clitic `l'`.
  * **expected** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The reading each word should have: `{word: reading}`, or
    `risk -> reading` to decide per occurrence (`risk.line`, `risk.word`,
    `risk.clitic`). A mapping names an elided form by its clitic
    (`{"est": "verb", "l'est": "noun"}`); `"est"` alone does not cover
    “l’Est”. Otherwise what a `detectors` entry found for that word on that
    line (e.g. [`voxy.speechtext.pos_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.pos_detector)), else None (just report).
  * **detectors** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)]]) – `text -> risks` proposers of expected readings.
  * **emitter** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The phoneme recogniser; default [`phoneme_emitter()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter).
  * **words_of** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]]) – `audio -> timed words`; default ASR (`voxy.refprep.transcribe`).
  * **scoring** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – How a reading is scored in the audio ([`SCORERS`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.SCORERS)).
    `"phrase"` (default): as the whole phrase around the word, its
    `context` neighbours written out with `phonemize`
    ([`phrase_scorer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phrase_scorer)). `"spot"`: spotted in that window
    ([`spot_scorer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.spot_scorer)). `"crop"`: the word alone, cut at its ASR times
    ([`crop_scorer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.crop_scorer)). Only the options that scoring takes are used.
  * **phonemize** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – For `"phrase"`; default [`espeak_phonemizer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.espeak_phonemizer).
  * **context** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Words kept on each side of the flagged one.
  * **margin** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – See [`Verdict.decided`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verdict.decided); default `scorer.margin`.
  * **scorer** ([`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A ready [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer); wins over `scoring` and its options.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)]

Returns the findings in text order; `[f for f in findings if f.ok is False]` are
the words decidedly misread (re-render those), `f.ok is None` ones were not
decided or not found.

* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – Before any ASR or scoring, when `expected` names a word or a
      reading the readings table does not have (a mapping is checked whole, so
      a key typo is caught too). A detector’s proposal naming no reading of its
      word is dropped instead, with a warning: that word is reported, not checked.
* **Return type:**
  [*list*](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[*Finding*](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)]

### voxy.pronounce.audit_verifier(lines, \*, emitter=None, words_of=<function \_transcribed_words>, scorer='phrase', margin=None, \*\*audit_options)

A [`Verifier`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verifier) over [`audit()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.audit), for the `lines` that will be rendered.

`audit_options` are `audit`’s own (`readings`, `expected`, `detectors`,
`language`…), applied to one line at a time, so an `expected` function sees
the risk with its real line number. The `detectors` run once on all the lines, so
they read a sentence that spans two lines in context; the risks they propose for a
line outside the text are dropped. `emitter`, `words_of`, `scorer` and
`margin` are the defaults for `audit`’s.

* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – Here, before anything is rendered, when `expected` names a word
      or a reading the readings table does not have (with the real line number
      for an `expected` function), or when a line holds a newline. A detector’s
      proposal naming no reading is dropped with a warning, as in `audit`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)]]

### voxy.pronounce.best_reading(log_probs, vocab, readings, , blank=None)

The name of the reading `log_probs` support best.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line(risks, , readings, expected=None)

[`checks_from_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_from_risks), grouped by the line each risk is on.

Legacy: `render_verified`’s default verifier finds and tells apart the
occurrences itself; this feeds its `checks=` adapter.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]]

### voxy.pronounce.checks_from_risks(risks, , readings, expected=None)

`verify_words` checks for the flagged words that have known IPA readings.

Legacy: [`audit()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.audit) (`render_verified`’s default verifier) does this per
occurrence; this feeds `render_verified`’s `checks=` adapter.

`readings` maps a word (case-insensitively) to `{name: IPA}`, e.g. from a
Lexique-derived heteronym list the caller supplies; `expected` names the
reading each word should have, and otherwise the risks’ own `expected` (what a
detector such as `voxy.speechtext.pos_detector` found) is used. Words with no
entry are skipped, and so are words elided onto a clitic (a risk with a `clitic`,
“l’Est”), whose differing reading then leaves the word’s open: `verify_words`
matches spellings, not places (`render_verified`’s default verifier checks
places). Each word is checked once: `verify_words` finds every place
it is spoken, so a word whose risks name *different* readings gets none here
(group the risks by line with [`checks_by_line()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line) to check each one).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]

### voxy.pronounce.checks_verifier(checks, \*, emitter=None, words_of=<function \_transcribed_words>, scorer='phrase', margin=None)

A [`Verifier`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verifier) for legacy `checks` ([`checks_by_line()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line)): words by spelling.

A checked word ASR never found is a finding without a verdict.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)]]

### voxy.pronounce.close_phonemes()

Stop the recogniser workers (free their memory).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.pronounce.crop_scorer(, emitter, padding=0.08, margin=0.5)

The word alone, cut at its ASR times (`padding` each side), scored by
[`score_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.score_readings); ASR word times are often too loose for this.

* **Return type:**
  [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer)

### voxy.pronounce.ctc_log_likelihood(log_probs, target, , blank=0)

`log P(target | log_probs)` under CTC (the forward algorithm, in log space).

`log_probs` is `frames x vocab` (log-softmax). `-inf` when the target cannot
be aligned (more symbols than frames allow).

```pycon
>>> lp = log_probs_from_path([1, 2], vocab_size=3)
>>> ctc_log_likelihood(lp, [1, 2]) > ctc_log_likelihood(lp, [2, 1])
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### voxy.pronounce.espeak_phonemizer(, model='facebook/wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft', threads=None, rootdir=None)

The default [`Phonemizer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Phonemizer): espeak-ng (bundled by `espeakng-loader`), run in
the recogniser’s env, so its IPA is the recogniser’s own alphabet.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### voxy.pronounce.failing(verdicts)

The verdicts whose word was decidedly read the wrong way (`ok is False`).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Verdict`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verdict)]

### voxy.pronounce.heteronym_readings(language='fr')

voxy’s own heteronym table for `language`: `{word: {reading name: IPA}}`.

A short, hand-made list (French: *est*, *fils*, *plus*, *tous*, the  *-ent* verbs…);
merge a fuller one: `{**voxy.lexique.cached_lexique_heteronyms(path), **heteronym_readings()}`
(Lexique-derived, the hand-made readings winning), or one read with [`load_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.load_readings).

```pycon
>>> heteronym_readings("fr")["est"]["noun"]
'ɛst'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### voxy.pronounce.known_symbols(ipa, vocab)

The symbols of `ipa` the recogniser knows, longest first; stress marks, spaces
and anything else it never emits are dropped.

```pycon
>>> known_symbols("ˈtʁist ɛ", ["<pad>", "t", "ʁ", "i", "s", "ɛ"])
['t', 'ʁ', 'i', 's', 't', 'ɛ']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.pronounce.load_readings(path)

Heteronym readings `{word: {reading name: IPA}}` from a caller’s file.

A `.json` file holds that mapping; any other file is tab-separated
`word<TAB>reading name<TAB>IPA`, one reading per line (`#` lines and blank
lines skipped), e.g. a list derived from Lexique (`voxy.lexique.cached_lexique_heteronyms`
builds one from your copy; voxy ships no Lexique data).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### voxy.pronounce.log_probs_from_path(path, , vocab_size, confidence=0.9)

Log-probabilities of a recogniser that hears `path` (one id per frame).

A test and doctest helper: each frame gives `confidence` to its id and shares
the rest evenly.

```pycon
>>> log_probs_from_path([0], vocab_size=2).round(2).tolist()
[[-0.11, -2.3]]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.pronounce.normal_word(word)

`word` as compared with ASR words: stripped, edge punctuation off, casefolded.

```pycon
>>> normal_word(" Smith’s,")
"smith's"
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter(, model='facebook/wav2vec2-lv-60-espeak-cv-ft', threads=None, rootdir=None)

The default [`Emitter`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Emitter): the wav2vec2 phoneme recogniser in its own env.

The env (torch, transformers) is built on first use under the data root, and the
model weights download from the Hugging Face hub then.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]

### voxy.pronounce.phrase_readings(log_probs, vocab, readings, , before='', after='', blank=None)

Each reading’s CTC log-likelihood as the whole phrase `before + reading + after`.

The words around the flagged one are written out (IPA) and are the same in every
candidate, so the comparison isolates the word: its neighbours’ sounds cannot be
credited to a longer reading, as they are when the word is cropped or spotted alone.

```pycon
>>> vocab = ["<pad>", "ɛ", "s", "t", "l", "ə"]
>>> lp = log_probs_from_path([2, 3, 1, 4, 5], vocab_size=6)  # "(trist)e" s t ɛ l ə
>>> s = phrase_readings(lp, vocab, {"verb": "ɛ", "noun": "ɛst"}, before="st", after="lə")
>>> s["verb"] > s["noun"]
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.pronounce.phrase_scorer(, emitter, phonemize=None, language='fr', elisions=None, context=1, padding=0.08, margin=2.0)

Each reading as the whole phrase around the word ([`phrase_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phrase_readings)), the
`context` words on each side written out by `phonemize` in `language`.

The neighbours are the same in every candidate, so only the word decides.
`phonemize` defaults to [`espeak_phonemizer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.espeak_phonemizer) (its worker starts on the first
call); it must give one IPA per text, or a `ValueError` is raised. An elided
clitic next to the word (`l'` before `Est`) is written from `elisions`
(default `ELISIONS[language]`, see [`spoken_context()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.spoken_context)).

* **Return type:**
  [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer)

### voxy.pronounce.reading_name(name)

The reading a name stands for: `"verb~liaison"` is a variant of `"verb"`.

```pycon
>>> reading_name("verb~liaison"), reading_name("noun")
('verb', 'noun')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.pronounce.reading_scorer(scoring='phrase', \*\*options)

The [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer) named `scoring` in [`SCORERS`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.SCORERS), made with `options`.

```pycon
>>> reading_scorer("crop", emitter=None).margin
0.5
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer)

### voxy.pronounce.render_verified(lines, \*, render, verify=None, checks=None, emitter=None, words_of=<function \_transcribed_words>, max_attempts=3, scorer='phrase', margin=None)

Render each line, and re-render the ones whose flagged words came out wrong.

After each render, `verify(text, audio, line)` says what the audio did with each
flagged word ([`Finding`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)); the line is rendered again while a word is
decidedly misread (`f.ok is False`), up to `max_attempts` renders. A blank line
is not rendered (line numbers still count it, as `flag_risks` does).
[`LineTakes.chosen`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.LineTakes.chosen) is the take to keep; [`LineTakes.verified`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.LineTakes.verified) also
requires each expected reading to be confirmed (a word ASR did not find, or the
recogniser could not decide, leaves the line unverified rather than retried).

* **Parameters:**
  * **lines** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The lines to speak, in order (line numbers start at 1).
  * **render** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)]) – `(text, line, attempt) -> audio path`; each call should give a
    new take (a new seed, or a service’s own variation).
    [`speech_renderer()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.speech_renderer) adapts a [`voxy.base.SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel).
  * **verify** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Finding`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Finding)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A [`Verifier`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verifier). Default [`audit_verifier()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.audit_verifier) `(lines)`, which
    flags the line’s heteronyms itself and tells the occurrences of a word
    apart (“l’Est” from “est”); build it yourself to pass `audit`’s options
    (`readings`, `expected`, `detectors`…).
  * **checks** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Legacy, instead of `verify`: by line number, the words to check by
    spelling ([`checks_by_line()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_by_line)); [`checks_verifier()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_verifier) adapts them.
  * **emitter** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The phoneme recogniser for a `scorer` given by name; default
    [`phoneme_emitter()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter).
  * **words_of** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]]) – `audio -> timed words`; the default transcribes with
    `voxy.refprep.transcribe`.
  * **max_attempts** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Renders of one line at most.
  * **scorer** ([`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – As in [`audit()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.audit) (default: phrase scoring, its neighbours
    written out by the real espeak worker, so offline tests inject
    `phrase_scorer(emitter=..., phonemize=fake)` or use `"crop"`). They
    default the default verifier and `checks`; a `verify` has its own.
  * **margin** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – As in [`audit()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.audit) (default: phrase scoring, its neighbours
    written out by the real espeak worker, so offline tests inject
    `phrase_scorer(emitter=..., phonemize=fake)` or use `"crop"`). They
    default the default verifier and `checks`; a `verify` has its own.
* **Raises:**
  [**ValueError**](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#ValueError) – For a bad `max_attempts`, both `verify` and `checks`, or (from
      [`audit_verifier()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.audit_verifier), when it is built) an expected reading the readings
      table does not have: all before the first render.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`LineTakes`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.LineTakes)]

```pycon
>>> heard = {"est": "ɛ"}  # a fake recogniser: what each word sounds like
>>> def emitter(audio, start, end):
...     vocab = ["<pad>", "ɛ", "s", "t", "l"]
...     path = [vocab.index(s) for s in "l" + heard["est"]]
...     return log_probs_from_path(path, vocab_size=5), vocab
>>> def render(text, line, attempt):
...     heard["est"] = "ɛst" if attempt else "ɛ"  # the second take is right
...     return f"take-{line}-{attempt}.wav"
>>> words = lambda audio: [{"start": 0.0, "end": 0.1, "text": "L'"},
...                        {"start": 0.1, "end": 0.3, "text": "Est"}]
>>> phonemize = lambda texts, language: ["l" for _ in texts]  # a fake espeak
>>> scorer = phrase_scorer(emitter=emitter, phonemize=phonemize)
>>> verify = audit_verifier(["L'Est"], words_of=words, scorer=scorer,
...                         readings={"est": {"verb": "ɛ", "noun": "ɛst"}},
...                         expected={"l'est": "noun"})
>>> [result] = render_verified(["L'Est"], render=render, verify=verify)
>>> [t.audio for t in result.takes], result.chosen.attempt, result.verified
(['take-1-0.wav', 'take-1-1.wav'], 1, True)
```

### voxy.pronounce.score_readings(log_probs, vocab, readings, , blank=None)

Each reading’s CTC log-likelihood per target symbol (higher is better).

Normalising by length keeps a longer reading (“ɛst”) from losing to a shorter one
(“ɛ”) just for having more symbols to pay for. `blank` defaults to the id of
[`BLANK_SYMBOL`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.BLANK_SYMBOL) in `vocab` (0 if it has none).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.pronounce.speech_renderer(model, voice=None, , outdir=None, take_kwarg=None, \*\*synthesize_kwargs)

A `render` for [`render_verified()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.render_verified) over a [`voxy.base.SpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.base.html.md#voxy.base.SpeechModel).

Each take is saved as `<outdir>/<line>-<attempt>.<format>` (default outdir: a
new folder per renderer under `voxy_cache_dir("takes")`, so runs never
overwrite each other’s takes). With `take_kwarg` (e.g. `"seed"`), the attempt
number is passed to `model.synthesize` under that name, so a seeded model gives
a new take; without it, the model is simply called again.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.pronounce.split_elisions(words, , elisions=())

Timed words split at each elision of `elisions`, as `_text_words()` splits
the text, so [`align_words()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.align_words) can match them.

Whisper’s `" l" | "'est"` becomes `" l'" | "est"` (the apostrophe moved back);
a word heard whole, `" l'est"`, becomes `" l'"` (empty, at its start) and
`"est"` (its whole span). Other apostrophes (an English opening quote) are left
alone.

```pycon
>>> words = [{"text": " à", "start": 0, "end": 1}, {"text": " l", "start": 1, "end": 2},
...          {"text": "'est", "start": 2, "end": 3}, {"text": " l'est", "start": 3, "end": 4},
...          {"text": " 'War", "start": 4, "end": 5}]
>>> [(w["text"], w["start"], w["end"]) for w in split_elisions(words, elisions={"l'": "l"})]
[(' à', 0, 1), (" l'", 1, 2), ('est', 2, 3), (" l'", 3, 3), ('est', 3, 4), (" 'War", 4, 5)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.pronounce.spoken_context(words, , elisions=None)

`(text, tail)`: what `words` say, for a phonemizer, and the IPA of an elided
clitic they end with.

A clitic of `elisions` (`{clitic: IPA}`, e.g. `ELISIONS["fr"]`) that ASR split
from its word is joined back to it, whichever side the apostrophe went
(`L'` | `homme`, or Whisper’s `l` | `'aube`). One left at the end (its word
is the flagged one, or outside the window) is written from `elisions` instead of
being left to the phonemizer, which reads a standalone `l'` as /ɛl/. Anything
not in `elisions` (an English quote, `James'`) is left as it is.

```pycon
>>> fr = {"l'": "l", "d'": "d"}
>>> spoken_context([{"text": " L'"}, {"text": " homme,"}, {"text": " d’"}], elisions=fr)
("L'homme", 'd')
>>> spoken_context([{"text": " avant"}, {"text": " l"}, {"text": "'aube."}], elisions=fr)
("avant l'aube", '')
>>> spoken_context([{"text": " read"}, {"text": " 'War"}], elisions=fr)
("read 'War", '')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.pronounce.spot_log_likelihood(log_probs, target, , blank=0, filler_penalty=None)

`log P` of `target` said somewhere in `log_probs`, the rest being filler.

Keyword spotting under CTC: frames before and after the target are explained by a
filler that takes each frame’s best symbol at a cost of `filler_penalty` nats.
Scoring a word inside a window that holds its neighbours, a reading wins by
matching phonemes that are really there, not by the window’s edges: a crop cut
from loose ASR word times otherwise favours the longer reading (/ɛst/ over /ɛ/).

```pycon
>>> vocab = ["<pad>", "ɛ", "s", "t", "l"]
>>> lp = log_probs_from_path([4, 1, 0, 4], vocab_size=5)  # "l ɛ l": the verb
>>> verb, noun = (spot_log_likelihood(lp, tokenize_phonemes(r, vocab)) for r in ("ɛ", "ɛst"))
>>> verb > noun
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### voxy.pronounce.spot_readings(log_probs, vocab, readings, , blank=None, filler_penalty=None)

Each reading’s [`spot_log_likelihood()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.spot_log_likelihood), less that of filler alone (higher is better).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.pronounce.spot_scorer(, emitter, context=1, padding=0.08, filler_penalty=1.0, margin=2.0)

The reading spotted in the window of `context` words on each side, the rest
left to filler ([`spot_readings()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.spot_readings)); a neighbour’s /s/ or /t/ can still be
credited to the longer reading.

* **Return type:**
  [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer)

### voxy.pronounce.timed_words(segments)

The timed words of ASR segments (`voxy.refprep.transcribe`’s output).

Words without times are dropped; a segment with no timed word counts as one word.

```pycon
>>> timed_words([{"words": [{"start": 0.0, "end": 0.2, "text": "a"},
...                         {"start": None, "end": None, "text": "b"}]},
...              {"start": 1.0, "end": 2.0, "text": "c", "words": []}])
[{'start': 0.0, 'end': 0.2, 'text': 'a'}, {'start': 1.0, 'end': 2.0, 'text': 'c'}]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]

### voxy.pronounce.tokenize_phonemes(reading, vocab)

Vocabulary ids of an IPA `reading`, longest symbol first; spaces are ignored.

A reading may also be given as a sequence of symbols. Raises `ValueError` on a
symbol the recogniser does not know, since it could never be heard.

```pycon
>>> tokenize_phonemes("ɛ̃s", ["<pad>", "ɛ", "ɛ̃", "s"])
[2, 3]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.pronounce.verify_words(audio, checks, , words, emitter=None, scorer='phrase', margin=None)

Verdicts for each `(word, readings, expected)` at each place ASR found it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The render.
  * **checks** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]) – The words to check, each with its candidate readings
    (`{name: IPA}`) and the reading it should have (or None to just
    report). [`checks_from_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.checks_from_risks) builds them from `flag_risks`.
  * **words** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]) – Timed words of the render (`transcribe(audio)`’s segments’ words).
  * **emitter** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(audio, start, end) -> (log_probs, vocab)` for a `scorer`
    given by name; default [`phoneme_emitter()`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.phoneme_emitter).
  * **scorer** ([`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer) | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – How each reading is scored: a [`Scorer`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Scorer), or a name in
    [`SCORERS`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.SCORERS) (default `"phrase"`: the whole phrase around the word,
    its neighbours written out by the real espeak worker, so offline tests
    inject `phrase_scorer(emitter=..., phonemize=fake)` or use `"crop"`).
  * **margin** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – See [`Verdict.decided`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verdict.decided); default `scorer.margin`.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Verdict`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#voxy.pronounce.Verdict)]

### voxy.pronounce.word_indices(words, word)

Indices of the ASR words matching `word` (case and punctuation aside).

```pycon
>>> word_indices([{"text": " Il"}, {"text": " est,"}, {"text": "Est"}], "est")
[1, 2]
>>> word_indices([{"text": " est…"}], "est")
[0]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.pronounce.word_spans(words, word)

`(start, end)` of every ASR word matching `word` (case and punctuation aside).

`words` are timed words as `voxy.refprep.transcribe` gives them
(`{"start", "end", "text", ...}`).

```pycon
>>> word_spans([{"start": 0.1, "end": 0.3, "text": " Est,"}], "est")
[(0.1, 0.3)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]


# _autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md

# voxy.refprep

Prepare a speaker’s recordings for cloning and fine-tuning: clean, cut, transcribe, score.

```pycon
>>> from voxy import refprep
>>> clips = refprep.prepare_reference(["tape1.m4a", "tape2.mp3"], voice="ada")
>>> ref = refprep.best_references(clips)[0]
>>> ref["path"], ref["text"], ref["score"]
```

The steps, each a function you can call alone or replace:

1. `condition` (ffmpeg): any format to mono PCM WAV at `sample_rate`, with a
   high-pass, optional denoising (`denoise=`: ‘afftdn’, ‘anlmdn’, ‘deepfilternet’, or None) and
   loudness normalisation (EBU R128, `loudness_lufs`).
2. `transcribe`: timed segments and words from a local Whisper (scribed’s
   faster-whisper backend, in its own environment, see `voxy.envs`).
3. `speaker` (optional, `voxy.speakers.speaker_filter`): marks words, and
   untranscribed stretches, spoken by someone other than the target voice.
4. `plan_clips`: cut points at sentence/segment boundaries, so each clip is
   `min_seconds`-`max_seconds` long, carries its exact text, and never
   contains a marked word.
5. `score_clip`: duration, signal-to-noise estimate, clipping, level, ASR
   confidence, speaking rate and (with a speaker step) the speaker match,
   folded into a `score` in [0, 1].

`prepare_reference` runs them all and saves the clips plus `manifest.jsonl` in
the voice’s samples store (`voxy.stores.samples_store`), so any backend (a
reference clip) and fine-tuning (`voxy.finetune`, the whole set) read the same data.
It only ever adds to the store, keeping every run; `latest_runs` gives each source’s
latest run, and `forget` is the one function that deletes clips.

### Module Attributes

| [`SPEAKER_SCORE_RANGE`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.SPEAKER_SCORE_RANGE)   | Speaker similarity mapped to the score's `speaker` part (0 at the low end, 1 at the high).                                                                   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`SLUG_PATTERN`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.SLUG_PATTERN)          | The slugs this module gives sources (see `_slug`), and the clip keys made from them.                                                                         |
| [`RUN_ID_TIME_FORMAT`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.RUN_ID_TIME_FORMAT)    | its UTC start time to the microsecond, plus random hex characters, so ids sort by time and two runs never share one.                                         |
| [`LEGACY_RUN`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.LEGACY_RUN)            | `forget(..., run=LEGACY_RUN)` selects entries written before runs were recorded (no `run` field), matching even a relative `source` exactly as it was typed. |
| [`DENOISE_FILTERS`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.DENOISE_FILTERS)       | no denoising).                                                                                                                                               |
| [`DF_SAMPLE_RATE`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.DF_SAMPLE_RATE)        | DeepFilterNet works at 48 kHz; it needs an old torch/torchaudio pair, hence its own env.                                                                     |

### Functions

| [`best_references`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.best_references)(manifest, \*[, n, ...])            | The `n` best clips for zero-shot reference (length in range, best score first).                                                                                                                           |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`close_asr`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.close_asr)()                                        | Stop the transcription workers (free their memory).                                                                                                                                                       |
| [`condition`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.condition)(src, dst, \*[, sample_rate, start, ...]) | Convert `src` (any format ffmpeg reads) to clean mono 16-bit WAV at `dst`.                                                                                                                                |
| [`conditioning_filters`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.conditioning_filters)(\*[, denoise, ...])           | The ffmpeg audio filter chain for `condition`.                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`deepfilternet_denoise`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.deepfilternet_denoise)(src, dst, \*[, ...])         | Denoise the 48 kHz WAV `src` into `dst` with DeepFilterNet 3.                                                                                                                                             |
| [`forget`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.forget)(samples, source, \*[, run, dry_run, log])   | Remove `source`'s clips (only those of one `run`, if given) from a samples store: its manifest entries, their clip keys and the source's conditioned key.                                                 |
| [`latest_runs`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.latest_runs)(manifest)                              | `manifest` with, per source, only the entries of its most recent run.                                                                                                                                     |
| [`load_manifest`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.load_manifest)(samples)                             | The manifest saved by `prepare_reference` in a samples store.                                                                                                                                             |
| [`partial_transcribe`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.partial_transcribe)([rootdir])                      | The default transcriber, bound to a data root.                                                                                                                                                            |
| [`plan_clips`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.plan_clips)(segments, \*[, min_seconds, ...])       | Clips `[{start, end, text, words}]` cut between words, ending sentences where possible.                                                                                                                   |
| [`prepare_reference`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.prepare_reference)(sources, \*[, voice, ...])       | Condition, transcribe, cut and score `sources`; save clips and manifest; return it.                                                                                                                       |
| [`score_clip`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.score_clip)(samples, sample_rate, \*[, words, ...]) | Quality measures of a clip, and their combination `score` in [0, 1].                                                                                                                                      |
| [`summarize`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.summarize)(manifest)                                | Totals for a manifest: clips, minutes, minutes above score thresholds.                                                                                                                                    |
| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.transcribe)(audio, \*[, language, model, ...])      | Timed segments `[{start, end, text, confidence, words: [...]}, ...]` of `audio`.                                                                                                                          |
| [`transcribe_text`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.transcribe_text)(audio, \*\*kwargs)                 | The transcript of `audio` as one string.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| [`unique_slugs`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.unique_slugs)(sources, \*[, reserved])              | One distinct slug per source: the file's stem, plus parent folders only within a group of sources sharing a stem (stem tracks: every one is `vocals.wav`), numbered where folders cannot tell them apart. |
| [`with_deepfilternet`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.with_deepfilternet)([conditioner, denoiser, ...])   | A `conditioner` that denoises with DeepFilterNet between two ffmpeg passes.                                                                                                                               |

### voxy.refprep.DENOISE_FILTERS *= {'afftdn': ['afftdn=nr=12:nf=-50:tn=1'], 'anlmdn': ['anlmdn=s=0.0005'], 'deepfilternet': [], None: []}*

no denoising).

* **Type:**
  ffmpeg filters for each `denoise` strategy (None

### voxy.refprep.DF_SAMPLE_RATE *= 48000*

DeepFilterNet works at 48 kHz; it needs an old torch/torchaudio pair, hence its own env.

### voxy.refprep.LEGACY_RUN *= 'legacy'*

`forget(..., run=LEGACY_RUN)` selects entries written before runs were recorded
(no `run` field), matching even a relative `source` exactly as it was typed.
Older voxy rewrote the whole manifest on every call, so such entries all come from
one call, in one folder: a relative string among them names one file.

### voxy.refprep.RUN_ID_TIME_FORMAT *= '%Y%m%dT%H%M%S.%fZ'*

its UTC start time to the microsecond, plus
random hex characters, so ids sort by time and two runs never share one.

* **Type:**
  A run id (`run` in each manifest entry)

### voxy.refprep.SLUG_PATTERN *= re.compile('[a-z0-9-]+')*

The slugs this module gives sources (see `_slug`), and the clip keys made from them.

### voxy.refprep.SPEAKER_SCORE_RANGE *= (0.3, 0.7)*

Speaker similarity mapped to the score’s `speaker` part (0 at the low end, 1 at the high).

### voxy.refprep.best_references(manifest, , n=3, min_seconds=5.0, max_seconds=12.0, min_score=0.0, latest_only=True)

The `n` best clips for zero-shot reference (length in range, best score first).

With `latest_only` (the default) it picks from `latest_runs(manifest)`: an older
run of a source is the same audio cut again, so its clips would come back as
near-duplicates of the newer ones, and the newer run is the one made with the
current settings. A reference saved from an older run stays valid either way (its
key and bytes are kept); pass `latest_only=False` to choose among every run.

```pycon
>>> m = [{"duration": 8, "score": 0.7}, {"duration": 2, "score": 0.9},
...      {"duration": 10, "score": 0.8}]
>>> [c["score"] for c in best_references(m, n=2)]
[0.8, 0.7]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

Denoise the 48 kHz WAV `src` into `dst` with DeepFilterNet 3.

### voxy.refprep.forget(samples, source, \*, run=None, dry_run=False, log=<built-in function print>)

Remove `source`’s clips (only those of one `run`, if given) from a samples
store: its manifest entries, their clip keys and the source’s conditioned key.
Returns the deleted keys (with `dry_run=True`: the keys it would delete, changing
nothing).

The only function in voxy that deletes voice samples (`prepare_reference` never
does), so it is careful about what it deletes:

- entries match `source` by real path: their `source_path`, or, for entries an
  older voxy wrote without one, their `source` only if it is absolute. A relative
  `source` names whatever file had that name where that run started, so such
  entries never match; they are logged, and `run=LEGACY_RUN` removes them
  deliberately (matching `source` exactly as recorded, as in
  `forget(samples, "vocals.wav", run=LEGACY_RUN)`);
- only keys of the form this module writes (`clips/<slug>-NNNN.wav`,
  `conditioned/<slug>.wav`), with a slug taken from a matched entry’s clip key, are
  deleted, never a top-level sample;
- a key a remaining entry names, or whose slug a remaining entry uses, is kept;
- one writer at a time: two processes changing one store at once can lose a
  manifest update (the store has no lock);
- the manifest is read just before it is written, and written first, so an
  interruption leaves unlisted files, never a manifest naming deleted ones.

```pycon
>>> store = {"clips/a-0001.wav": b"A", "conditioned/a.wav": b"C",
...          "clips/b-0001.wav": b"B", "tape1.wav": b"T"}
>>> store[MANIFEST_KEY] = _dump_manifest([
...     {"key": "clips/a-0001.wav", "slug": "a", "source": "/s/a.wav"},
...     {"key": "clips/b-0001.wav", "slug": "b", "source": "/s/b.wav"},
...     {"key": "tape1.wav", "source": "/s/a.wav"}])
>>> forget(store, "/s/a.wav", dry_run=True)
['clips/a-0001.wav', 'conditioned/a.wav']
>>> len(load_manifest(store)), len(store)
(3, 5)
>>> forget(store, "/s/a.wav")
['clips/a-0001.wav', 'conditioned/a.wav']
>>> [e["key"] for e in load_manifest(store)], sorted(store)
(['clips/b-0001.wav'], ['clips/b-0001.wav', 'manifest.jsonl', 'tape1.wav'])
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.refprep.latest_runs(manifest)

`manifest` with, per source, only the entries of its most recent run.

`prepare_reference` keeps every run, so a source processed twice is in the
manifest twice (the same audio, cut again); consumers that want one copy of each
recording (training sets, reference picks, summaries) read this. Sources are told
apart by real path (`source_path`, or an absolute `source`); entries with no
`run` count as one run older than any recorded one; entries whose source cannot
be known (none, or a relative path from an older voxy) are all kept. Order is kept.
A source whose newest run gave no clips keeps its older run’s entries.

```pycon
>>> m = [{"key": "a1", "source_path": "/a", "run": "20260101T000000.000000Z-x"},
...      {"key": "a2", "source_path": "/a", "run": "20261101T000000.000000Z-y"},
...      {"key": "a0", "source_path": "/a"},
...      {"key": "b1", "source_path": "/b"},
...      {"key": "t", "source": "tape.wav"}]
>>> [e["key"] for e in latest_runs(m)]
['a2', 'b1', 't']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]

### voxy.refprep.load_manifest(samples)

The manifest saved by `prepare_reference` in a samples store.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.partial_transcribe(rootdir=None)

The default transcriber, bound to a data root.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]

### voxy.refprep.plan_clips(segments, , min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0, pad_seconds=0.12, total_seconds=None)

Clips `[{start, end, text, words}]` cut between words, ending sentences where possible.

Words accumulate until the clip passes `min_seconds` and a word ends a
sentence (or the next word would push it past `max_seconds`). Cuts fall in
the pause between two words, padded by up to `pad_seconds`. A word marked
`keep=False` (someone else’s, see `voxy.speakers`) ends the clip before it,
and the next clip starts after it.

```pycon
>>> w = lambda s, e, t: {"start": s, "end": e, "text": t, "confidence": 0.9}
>>> segs = [{"words": [w(0, 1, "One"), w(1.1, 2, "two."), w(3, 4, "Three"),
...                    w(4.1, 5, "four.")], "start": 0, "end": 5, "text": ""}]
>>> [c["text"] for c in plan_clips(segs, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=3)]
['One two.', 'Three four.']
>>> segs[0]["words"].insert(2, {**w(2.2, 2.6, " yes"), "keep": False})
>>> [(c["text"], c["start"]) for c in plan_clips(segs, min_seconds=1.5, max_seconds=3)]
[('One two.', 0.0), ('Three four.', 2.88)]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.prepare_reference(sources, \*, voice=None, samples=None, sample_rate=24000, denoise='afftdn', loudness_lufs=-20.0, min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0, language=None, transcriber=None, conditioner=None, speaker=None, rootdir=None, log=<built-in function print>)

Condition, transcribe, cut and score `sources`; save clips and manifest; return it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **sources** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)]) – Recordings, any format ffmpeg reads.
  * **voice** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Voice name: clips go to `samples_store(voice)`.
  * **samples** ([`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A store to write to instead (`filename -> bytes`).
  * **sample_rate** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **denoise** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **loudness_lufs** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Conditioning (see `condition`).
  * **min_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Clip length bounds.
  * **max_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Clip length bounds.
  * **language** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Force the ASR language (default: detected).
  * **transcriber** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(wav_path, language=) -> segments` (default `transcribe`).
  * **conditioner** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(src, dst, sample_rate=, filters=) -> path` (default `condition`).
  * **speaker** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(wav_path, segments) -> segments` marking other voices’ words
    (`voxy.speakers.speaker_filter`); None keeps every voice.
* **Returns:**
  one dict per clip (`key`, `path` if on disk, `text`,
  `source` as given, `source_path` (its real path), `slug`, `run` (one id
  per call), `start`, `end`, and the `score_clip` measures), best first,
  earlier runs’ entries included.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

It never deletes or overwrites anything in the store. Run again into the same store
(another recording, or the same file again), it gives this run’s sources fresh slugs
that no manifest entry and no clip or conditioned key in the store already uses, so
every earlier clip keeps its key and its bytes, and saved reference profiles
(`ref_audio` + `ref_text`) stay valid. The manifest keeps every earlier entry and
adds the new ones (re-read just before writing, so a `forget` or another run that
finished meanwhile is not undone). Re-processing a source therefore adds clips beside
its earlier ones; consumers read `latest_runs(manifest)` to see one run per source,
and `forget(samples, source, run=...)` removes the others explicitly. A file given
twice in one call (by real path) is processed once.

### voxy.refprep.score_clip(samples, sample_rate, , words=(), text='', min_seconds=3.0, max_seconds=12.0)

Quality measures of a clip, and their combination `score` in [0, 1].

- `snr_db`: loud-frame level minus quiet-frame level (speech vs floor).
- `clipped`: fraction of samples at full scale.
- `level_db`: level of the loud frames.
- `asr_confidence`: mean Whisper word probability (low: mumbling, noise, music).
- `chars_per_second`: speaking rate (outliers: bad alignment).
- `speaker_similarity`: lowest match of a word to the target voice (words
  annotated by `voxy.speakers`; None otherwise).

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> speechy = np.concatenate([0.3 * rng.standard_normal(40000), 0.001 * rng.standard_normal(8000)])
>>> s = score_clip(speechy, 8000, text="x" * 70)
>>> s["snr_db"] > 30, 0 < s["score"] <= 1
(True, True)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.refprep.summarize(manifest)

Totals for a manifest: clips, minutes, minutes above score thresholds.

```pycon
>>> summarize([{"duration": 60, "score": 0.9}, {"duration": 30, "score": 0.4}])
{'clips': 2, 'minutes': 1.5, 'minutes_score_0.5+': 1.0, 'minutes_score_0.7+': 1.0}
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.refprep.transcribe(audio, , language=None, model='large-v3-turbo', threads=None, rootdir=None)

Timed segments `[{start, end, text, confidence, words: [...]}, ...]` of `audio`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.refprep.transcribe_text(audio, \*\*kwargs)

The transcript of `audio` as one string.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.refprep.unique_slugs(sources, , reserved=())

One distinct slug per source: the file’s stem, plus parent folders only within a
group of sources sharing a stem (stem tracks: every one is `vocals.wav`), numbered
where folders cannot tell them apart. Slugs never climb past what separates a group,
and a source whose stem is unique keeps it.

```pycon
>>> unique_slugs(["/s/one/vocals.wav", "/s/two/vocals.wav", "/s/talk.m4a"])
['one-vocals', 'two-vocals', 'talk']
>>> unique_slugs(["/Users/x/audio/talk.m4a", "/Users/x/audio/talk.wav"])
['talk', 'talk-2']
>>> unique_slugs(["/s/a.wav", "/s/a.wav", "/s/a-2.wav"])
['a', 'a-3', 'a-2']
```

`reserved` slugs (already used in the store) are never given out:

```pycon
>>> unique_slugs(["/t/vocals.wav"], reserved=["vocals"])
['vocals-2']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### voxy.refprep.with_deepfilternet(conditioner=None, , denoiser=None, rootdir=None)

A `conditioner` that denoises with DeepFilterNet between two ffmpeg passes.

Pass 1 converts the source to a 48 kHz mono WAV (no filters); DeepFilterNet cleans
it; pass 2 applies the usual `filters` (high-pass, loudness) and resamples to
`sample_rate`. `conditioner` (default [`condition()`](_autosummary/voxy.refprep.html.md#voxy.refprep.condition)) does both ffmpeg passes.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

# voxy.say_model

Local speech with the macOS `say` command: free, offline, no API key, no deps.

Good for previews and drafts before spending credits on a cloud voice. Voices are
the system’s (`say -v '?'`): e.g. “Samantha”, “Daniel”, “Karen”.

```pycon
>>> SaySpeechModel(run=lambda *a, **k: None).dflt_voice
'Samantha'
```
