# _autosummary/voxy.script.html.md

# voxy.script

Render a cast script: text segments, each read by its own voice, one audio file per section.

For anything narrated by more than one voice (an audiobook with a narrator and a quoted
guide, a dialogue, a radio play). Three plain-data inputs, each a JSON-able mapping so a
person can edit them and the rest follows:

- the **script**: a list of sections `{"id", "title"?, "segments": [{"role", "text"}]}`;
- the **casting**: `{"roles": {role: voice name or None}, "takes": {section id: take},
  "default_role"?}`; a role mapped to `None` has no voice yet (its sections are listed,
  not rendered);
- the **voices**: voice name -> `{"backend"?, "init"?, "params"?, "tempo"?, "effect"?,
  "external"?}` plus how to load it (`"library": name`, `"reference": {"audio", "text"}`
  or `"voice": id-or-name` passed to the backend as is). `tempo` (pitch kept, rubberband)
  and `effect` (an ffmpeg audio filter) are finishing steps; `external` marks a voice
  synthesised elsewhere (`missing_takes` lists what it owes, `add_take` files the audio).

Files under `root`:

> segments/<key>.wav|json   one take of one segment; the key hashes (voice, settings,
> : spoken text, take number), so a take is never overwritten
>   and an edit makes a new one

> sections/<id>.mp3         a section’s takes joined: pauses, tempo, effect, loudness
> : (EBU R128) evened across voices, a gap where the voice changes

> index.json                per section: status, segments (key, role, voice), file, seconds

Render again after editing: only segments whose key changed are synthesised, and only
sections whose takes or finishing changed are rebuilt. A retake of a section is
`"takes": {"s1": 2}` in the casting (a `seed` in the voice’s params moves with the take).

```pycon
>>> script = [{"id": "s1", "segments": [{"role": "guide", "text": "Come."}, {"role": "author", "text": "I come."}]}]
>>> casting = {"roles": {"guide": "g", "author": "a"}}
>>> [(s["role"], s["voice"]) for s in plan_script(script, casting)[0]["segments"]]
[('guide', 'g'), ('author', 'a')]
```

### Functions

| [`add_take`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.add_take)(root, segment, audio, \*[, ...])       | File one take: `segments/<key>.wav` (`audio`: WAV bytes) and its `.json`.                           |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`finish_section`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.finish_section)(wavs, out, finish)               | Join takes (each `(wav path, voice spec)`) into one MP3 at `out`.                                   |
| [`lengthen_pauses`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.lengthen_pauses)(samples, sr, \*, tiers[, ...])  | `samples` (mono float array) with each inner pause lengthened by its tier's extra seconds.          |
| [`load_voice_profile`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.load_voice_profile)(spec, \*[, root])            | The voice to hand `synthesize` from a voices entry (see the module docstring).                      |
| [`missing_takes`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.missing_takes)(script, root, \*[, casting, ...]) | Segments with no take yet (by default only those of external voices), in script order.              |
| [`plan_script`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.plan_script)(script, casting, \*[, text_prep])   | Each section with its segments resolved: `{role, voice, text, tts_text, take}`.                     |
| [`render_script`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.render_script)(script, root, \*[, casting, ...]) | Render what is missing or changed, section by section in script order; return (and save) the index. |
| [`segment_key`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.segment_key)(segment, voice)                     | A take's identity: a hash of the voice (loading and settings), spoken text and take number.         |
| [`status`](_autosummary/voxy.script.html.md#voxy.script.status)(root)                                    | Progress from `index.json`: counts per status, total `seconds`, `segments_by_voice`.                |

### voxy.script.add_take(root, segment, audio, , generation_seconds=None)

File one take: `segments/<key>.wav` (`audio`: WAV bytes) and its `.json`.

`segment` is an entry of `missing_takes` (or the renderer’s own), with `key` and
`voice_spec`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### voxy.script.finish_section(wavs, out, finish)

Join takes (each `(wav path, voice spec)`) into one MP3 at `out`.

Per take: pauses, then tempo, effect and loudness; a silent gap follows each take but
the last. Needs `ffmpeg` (with rubberband for `tempo`).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.script.lengthen_pauses(samples, sr, , tiers, floor_db=-35.0)

`samples` (mono float array) with each inner pause lengthened by its tier’s extra seconds.

A pause is a run of 10 ms frames `floor_db` below the loud frames (95th percentile);
it is lengthened by repeating its own middle, so the room tone carries on. Leading and
trailing silence is left as is.

```pycon
>>> tone = np.sin(np.arange(8000) / 3.0).astype(np.float32)
>>> y = np.concatenate([tone, np.zeros(4000, np.float32), tone])  # 0.5 s pause at 8 kHz
>>> len(lengthen_pauses(y, 8000, tiers=[[0.4, 0.25]])) - len(y)
2000
```

### voxy.script.load_voice_profile(spec, , root=None)

The voice to hand `synthesize` from a voices entry (see the module docstring).

### voxy.script.missing_takes(script, root, , casting=None, voices=None, text_prep=None, external_only=True)

Segments with no take yet (by default only those of external voices), in script order.

Each is `{section, role, voice, text, tts_text, take, key, voice_spec}`: hand it to
whatever renders that voice, then file the audio with `add_take(root, segment, wav)`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.script.plan_script(script, casting, , text_prep=None)

Each section with its segments resolved: `{role, voice, text, tts_text, take}`.

`tts_text` is `text_prep(text)` (what is spoken; default: the text itself), so the
take’s key follows what the voice says, not the displayed text.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.script.render_script(script, root, \*, casting=None, voices=None, only=None, finish=None, text_prep=None, model_factory=None, voice_loader=<function load_voice_profile>, log=<built-in function print>)

Render what is missing or changed, section by section in script order; return (and save) the index.

* **Parameters:**
  * **script** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)]) – Sections `{"id", "title"?, "segments": [{"role", "text"}]}`.
  * **root** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The output folder; `casting` and `voices` default to its
    `casting.json` and `voices.json`.
  * **only** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Section ids to render (default all); the index still lists every section.
  * **finish** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Overrides of `DFLT_FINISH` (gap between voices, loudness, bitrate, pauses).
  * **text_prep** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `text -> spoken text` per segment (e.g. `voxy.speechtext` preparation).
  * **model_factory** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(backend, **init) -> SpeechModel` (default `voxy.create_speech_model`).
  * **voice_loader** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)) – `(voice spec, root=) -> voice` (default `load_voice_profile`).
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### voxy.script.segment_key(segment, voice)

A take’s identity: a hash of the voice (loading and settings), spoken text and take number.

`tempo` and `effect` are finishing steps, left out: changing them rebuilds the
section files without new takes.

```pycon
>>> a = segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 1}, {"params": {"seed": 1}})
>>> a == segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 1}, {"params": {"seed": 1}, "tempo": 0.8})
True
>>> a == segment_key({"tts_text": "Hi", "take": 2}, {"params": {"seed": 1}})
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### voxy.script.status(root)

Progress from `index.json`: counts per status, total `seconds`, `segments_by_voice`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)


# _autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md

# voxy.speakers

Keep one speaker: find their voice in a recording and mark everyone else’s words.

Recordings of a person are rarely just that person: an interviewer asks the
questions, someone says “yes” or “uh-huh” in the middle of an answer. A clone or a
fine-tune trained on those clips learns the other voices too. This module
compares the voice in short sliding windows with a **voice print** (the mean
ECAPA speaker embedding of the target) and marks every transcribed word, and
every untranscribed stretch of someone else’s voice, that does not match it:

```pycon
>>> from voxy import refprep, speakers
>>> print_ = speakers.voice_print("clean_answer.wav")
>>> refprep.prepare_reference(["interview.m4a"], voice="ada",
...                           speaker=speakers.speaker_filter(print_))
```

`plan_clips` then never puts a marked word, or the pause around one, inside a
clip. With no voice print, `speaker_filter()` takes each recording’s
**dominant** voice (an iterated centroid over its loud windows), which is right
for a talk or an interview where the target does most of the talking.

The embeddings come from SpeechBrain’s ECAPA-TDNN (Apache-2.0, VoxCeleb weights)
running in voxy’s isolated `speaker` environment (`SPEAKER_ENV`, built on
first use, see `voxy.envs`); everything after the embeddings is numpy, so the
logic below is testable with made-up vectors.

### Module Attributes

| [`DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY)    | Cosine similarity to the voice print below which a window is someone else.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB)   | neither voice.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [`DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS) | Untranscribed foreign stretches shorter than this are ignored (one window's wobble).                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS) | Margin added around a foreign stretch, so a cut never clips its edge into a clip.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [`DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP)        | A word with this share of its length inside a foreign stretch is not kept.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [`DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY)      | Inside a transcribed turn, a stretch is someone else's only below this (smoothed) match: one-second windows of old, noisy audio dip well below `DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY` on the target's own voice, so a turn that matches as a whole is only cut where the dip is deep. |
| [`DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS)      | Window similarities are averaged over this many neighbours before finding stretches.                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [`DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS)    | never kept.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

### Functions

| [`close_speaker`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.close_speaker)()                                   | Stop the embedding workers (free their memory).                                       |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`dominant_centroid`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.dominant_centroid)(vectors, \*[, iterations, ...]) | The voice heard most: re-centre on the windows most like the centroid, repeatedly.    |
| [`embed_windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.embed_windows)(audio, \*[, spans, window, ...])    | ECAPA embeddings of `window`-second windows every `hop` s of `audio`.                 |
| [`foreign_spans`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.foreign_spans)(windows, similarity, \*[, ...])     | Stretches where a loud window does not match the voice print, padded by `pad`.        |
| [`loud_mask`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.loud_mask)(windows, samples, sample_rate, \*)      | Windows with speech in them: loud frames within `margin_db` of the speech level.      |
| [`mark_speaker`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.mark_speaker)(segments, windows, similarity, \*)   | Annotate each timed word with `speaker_similarity` and `keep`; add gap markers.       |
| [`smooth`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.smooth)(similarity[, windows])                     | Moving average of `similarity` over `windows` neighbours (edges: the shorter mean).   |
| [`speaker_filter`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.speaker_filter)([target, threshold, ...])          | A `refprep.prepare_reference(speaker=...)` step: `(wav_path, segments) -> segments`.  |
| [`turn_similarity`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)(segments, windows, ...[, loud])   | Match of each transcribed segment (a turn) to `voice_print`, from its mean window.    |
| [`voice_print`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.voice_print)(audio, \*[, spans, embed])            | The voice print of `audio` (one recording or several): the dominant voice's centroid. |

### Classes

| [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)(times, vectors)   | Speaker embeddings of sliding windows: `times` (n, 2) seconds, unit `vectors` (n, d).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_DIP_SIMILARITY *= 0.15*

Inside a transcribed turn, a stretch is someone else’s only below this (smoothed) match:
one-second windows of old, noisy audio dip well below `DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY` on the
target’s own voice, so a turn that matches as a whole is only cut where the dip is deep.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_FOREIGN_PAD_SECONDS *= 0.15*

Margin added around a foreign stretch, so a cut never clips its edge into a clip.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY *= 0.45*

Cosine similarity to the voice print below which a window is someone else.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_FOREIGN_SECONDS *= 0.2*

Untranscribed foreign stretches shorter than this are ignored (one window’s wobble).

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_MIN_TURN_SECONDS *= 1.0*

never kept.

* **Type:**
  Turns shorter than this are too short to attribute (”Yes.”, ”Uh-huh”)

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_SILENCE_MARGIN_DB *= 25.0*

neither voice.

* **Type:**
  Windows this far below the recording’s speech level are silence

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_SMOOTH_WINDOWS *= 3*

Window similarities are averaged over this many neighbours before finding stretches.

### voxy.speakers.DFLT_WORD_OVERLAP *= 0.25*

A word with this share of its length inside a foreign stretch is not kept.

### *class* voxy.speakers.Windows(times, vectors)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Speaker embeddings of sliding windows: `times` (n, 2) seconds, unit `vectors` (n, d).

#### similarity(voice_print)

Cosine similarity of each window to `voice_print`.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.close_speaker()

Stop the embedding workers (free their memory).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### voxy.speakers.dominant_centroid(vectors, , iterations=6, quantile=0.5)

The voice heard most: re-centre on the windows most like the centroid, repeatedly.

Clustering fragments a noisy voice into several clusters; this converges on
the majority voice instead (it needs that voice to be more than half the windows
the first mean is computed from).

```pycon
>>> rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
>>> a, b = np.eye(4)[0], np.eye(4)[1]
>>> vs = np.array([_unit(a + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(4)) for _ in range(30)]
...             + [_unit(b + 0.1 * rng.standard_normal(4)) for _ in range(10)])
>>> bool(dominant_centroid(vs) @ a > 0.95)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.embed_windows(audio, , spans=None, window=1.0, hop=0.1, model='speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb', threads=None, rootdir=None)

ECAPA embeddings of `window`-second windows every `hop` s of `audio`.

`spans` restricts the windows to those `(start, end)` stretches (default:
the whole file). Any sample rate; the worker resamples to 16 kHz.

* **Return type:**
  [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)

### voxy.speakers.foreign_spans(windows, similarity, , threshold=0.45, loud=None, min_seconds=0.2, pad=0.15)

Stretches where a loud window does not match the voice print, padded by `pad`.

`threshold` is one similarity, or one per window.

Each window speaks for the `hop`-wide slot around its centre, so a short “yes”
marks about the length of the dip it causes, not a whole window.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(20)])
>>> sim = np.array([0.8] * 8 + [0.1] * 4 + [0.8] * 8)
>>> [[round(x, 2) for x in s] for s in foreign_spans(Windows(t, None), sim, pad=0)]
[[1.25, 1.65]]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]

### voxy.speakers.loud_mask(windows, samples, sample_rate, , margin_db=25.0)

Windows with speech in them: loud frames within `margin_db` of the speech level.

```pycon
>>> w = Windows(np.array([[0, 1], [1, 2]]), np.zeros((2, 3)))
>>> x = np.concatenate([0.3 * np.ones(8000), np.zeros(8000)])
>>> loud_mask(w, x, 8000).tolist()
[True, False]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.mark_speaker(segments, windows, similarity, , threshold=0.45, loud=None, turns=None, dip_threshold=0.15, min_turn_seconds=1.0, word_overlap=0.25, pad=0.15, min_seconds=0.2)

Annotate each timed word with `speaker_similarity` and `keep`; add gap markers.

Without `turns`, a word is kept when the windows centred inside it match the
voice print on average. With `turns` (one match per segment, see
[`turn_similarity()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)), a word is kept when its whole segment matches and lasts
at least `min_turn_seconds`, and its `speaker_similarity` is the segment’s;
inside a segment only a deep dip (below `dip_threshold`) counts as someone else,
and a one-word sentence (“Yes.”) must match the voice print on its own.
Either way a word is dropped when `word_overlap` of it lies in a foreign
stretch. Every foreign stretch is also added as an empty word with
`keep=False` (an untranscribed “uh-huh” has no word of its own), padded by up
to `pad` and trimmed back to the kept words around it, so `refprep.plan_clips`
never puts it inside a clip. A segment without word timings is judged as one word.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(40)])
>>> sim = np.array([0.8] * 15 + [0.1] * 5 + [0.8] * 20)
>>> w = lambda s, e, x: {"start": s, "end": e, "text": x}
>>> segs = [{"start": 0, "end": 4, "text": "a b",
...          "words": [w(0.5, 1.4, " a"), w(2.5, 3.8, " b")]}]
>>> out = mark_speaker(segs, Windows(t, None), sim)
>>> [(x["text"], x["keep"]) for x in out[0]["words"]], out[1]["words"][0]["end"]
([(' a', True), (' b', True)], 2.5)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.speakers.smooth(similarity, windows=3)

Moving average of `similarity` over `windows` neighbours (edges: the shorter mean).

```pycon
>>> smooth(np.array([1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0])).round(2).tolist()
[1.0, 0.67, 0.67, 0.67, 1.0]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.speakers.speaker_filter(target=None, , threshold=0.45, dip_threshold=0.15, smooth_windows=3, min_turn_seconds=1.0, embed=None, \*\*embed_kwargs)

A `refprep.prepare_reference(speaker=...)` step: `(wav_path, segments) -> segments`.

Decides per transcribed segment (a turn: [`turn_similarity()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.turn_similarity)), then cuts
deep dips inside kept turns and other voices between them ([`mark_speaker()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.mark_speaker)).

* **Parameters:**
  * **target** (`ndarray` | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – The voice print to keep (from [`voice_print()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.voice_print)); None takes each
    recording’s dominant voice.
  * **threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Cosine similarity a turn (or a stretch between turns) needs to
    count as the target.
  * **dip_threshold** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Smoothed similarity below which a stretch inside a kept turn
    is someone else.
  * **smooth_windows** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Neighbouring windows averaged before finding stretches.
  * **min_turn_seconds** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Shorter turns are never kept.
  * **embed** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Windows`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.Windows)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `(path, **embed_kwargs) -> Windows` (default [`embed_windows()`](_autosummary/voxy.speakers.html.md#voxy.speakers.embed_windows)).
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]]

### voxy.speakers.turn_similarity(segments, windows, voice_print, , loud=None)

Match of each transcribed segment (a turn) to `voice_print`, from its mean window.

Averaging the embeddings over a whole turn is far steadier than any one window
on noisy audio: it is what tells an interviewer’s question from an answer. None
for a segment with no (loud) window centred in it.

```pycon
>>> t = np.array([[i * 0.1, i * 0.1 + 1] for i in range(40)])
>>> v = np.array([np.eye(2)[0]] * 20 + [np.eye(2)[1]] * 20)
>>> turn_similarity([{"start": 0, "end": 2}, {"start": 2.6, "end": 4.4}],
...                 Windows(t, v), np.eye(2)[0])
[1.0, 0.0]
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]

### voxy.speakers.voice_print(audio, , spans=None, embed=None, \*\*embed_kwargs)

The voice print of `audio` (one recording or several): the dominant voice’s centroid.

Pass recordings (or `spans` of one) where the target speaks alone, and this is
simply their voice; over mixed recordings it is whoever speaks most.

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`


# _autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md

# voxy.speechtext

Display text vs speech text, and spotting words a model may misread.

A text a person reads and the text a model should be given are not always the same.
Measured case (French, a Qwen3-TTS clone): a verse line starting with a capitalised
verb, “Est parti” after a line “Mon frere”, was read as the noun /est/ (“l’Est”) in 4
of 4 takes; lowercased (“est parti”) it was read correctly in 4 of 4. The capital, not
the line break, is the trigger: line-initial “Est” tokenises like the noun in “l’Est”.
ASR checks cannot catch this (Whisper hears “est” either way), so the fix is upstream:

1. [`prepare_speech_text()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text) turns display text into speech text: it lowercases a
   *verse-initial* capital that does not start a sentence (keeping deliberate capitals:
   words also capitalised mid-line, or named in `keep`), then applies a per-language
   respelling table and proper-name aliases, and returns every change it made.
2. [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) lists the words of a text a model may misread (heteronyms you
   supply, e.g. from Lexique; more detectors plug in through `extra`), saying which
   ones sit where the capital trigger bites. [`pos_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.pos_detector) is one such
   detector: it tags the text and, for heteronyms whose part of speech picks the
   reading (French “est”: verb /ɛ/, noun /ɛst/), names the `expected` reading;
   [`llm_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.llm_detector) asks a language model for the risky words and their readings.

Engines differ in what they accept: for several local models text is the only lever
(they take no phonemes or SSML), so this is a text-level step; it plugs into
`LocalCloneSpeechModel(text_prep=...)`. Verifying the audio itself (phoneme
recognition of the flagged words) is [`voxy.pronounce`](_autosummary/voxy.pronounce.html.md#module-voxy.pronounce).

```pycon
>>> text = "Mon frere\nEst parti\nLoin d'ici."
>>> prepare_speech_text(text).speech
"Mon frere\nest parti\nloin d'ici."
>>> prepare_speech_text(text, keep={"Est", "Loin"}).speech == text
True
```

### voxy.speechtext.LLM_RISK_PROMPT *= 'You help a text-to-speech system avoid misreadings. Below is a $language text, its lines numbered. List the words a speech model may misread: heteronyms (words with more than one pronunciation, such as French "est" as a verb or as a noun), names, abbreviations. For each, give the line, the word exactly as written, short names of its possible readings, and the reading this context needs.\\n\\nAnswer with a JSON list only, one object per word:\\n[{"line": 2, "word": "est", "readings": ["verb", "noun"], "expected": "verb", "why": "..."}]\\nUse "expected": null when the context does not decide. Answer [] if nothing is risky.\\n\\n$text\\n'*

The prompt [`llm_detector()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.llm_detector) sends; `$language` and `$text` are filled in.

### voxy.speechtext.NOUN_CLITICS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]]* *= {'fr': ("l'", "d'")}*

those that can come
before its noun reading (“l’Est”, “vent d’est”). After the others (“c’est”, “s’est”,
“n’est”) only the verb fits, and flagging every “c’est” would swamp a French text.

* **Type:**
  Clitics after which a heteronym is still flagged, by language

### voxy.speechtext.flag_risks(text, , heteronyms=(), extra=(), clitics=())

Words of `text` a model may misread, in text order.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The text that will be spoken (run it through [`prepare_speech_text()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text)
    first to see what is left).
  * **heteronyms** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]] | [`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Words with more than one reading, as a collection or as
    `{word: readings}` (e.g. from Lexique). Matched case-insensitively.
  * **extra** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Risk`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.Risk)]]]) – More detectors, each `text -> risks` (a part-of-speech rule, an LLM
    proposer). Their risks are merged in by line.
  * **clitics** ([`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Clitics a heteronym may be elided onto and still be flagged
    (e.g. [`NOUN_CLITICS`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.NOUN_CLITICS)): “l’Est” is then the risk `Est` with
    `clitic="l'"`.
* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Risk`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.Risk)]

A heteronym that is capitalised at a line start where no sentence begins is flagged
with `line_initial_capital=True`: that is where the capital trigger bites.

### voxy.speechtext.llm_detector(, chat=None, language='French', prompt='You help a text-to-speech system avoid misreadings. Below is a $language text, its lines numbered. List the words a speech model may misread: heteronyms (words with more than one pronunciation, such as French "est" as a verb or as a noun), names, abbreviations. For each, give the line, the word exactly as written, short names of its possible readings, and the reading this context needs.\\n\\nAnswer with a JSON list only, one object per word:\\n[{"line": 2, "word": "est", "readings": ["verb", "noun"], "expected": "verb", "why": "..."}]\\nUse "expected": null when the context does not decide. Answer [] if nothing is risky.\\n\\n$text\\n', clitics=("l'", "d'", "j'", "m'", "t'", "s'", "n'", "c'", "qu'", "jusqu'", "lorsqu'", "puisqu'", "quoiqu'"))

A [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) `extra` detector that asks a language model for risky words.

The model’s proposals are kept only when the word is really on the line it names,
and an `expected` reading only when it is one of the proposed `readings`; a
reply that is not a JSON list proposes nothing.

* **Parameters:**
  * **chat** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `prompt -> reply text`; default `aix.chat` (`pip install 'voxy[aix]'`,
    keys and model from aix’s own config). Each call costs a model request.
  * **language** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The text’s language, named in the prompt.
  * **prompt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – A `string.Template` with `$language` and `$text` (numbered lines).
  * **clitics** ([`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The clitics a word is elided onto in `language` (as `pos_detector`); a proposal for
    “l’Est” (or for “Est”, when the line only has it elided) carries the
    `clitic`, as [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) gives it.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Risk`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.Risk)]]

```pycon
>>> fake = lambda prompt: '[{"line": 1, "word": "est", "readings": ["verb", "noun"], "expected": "verb"}]'
>>> [(r.line, r.word, r.expected) for r in llm_detector(chat=fake)("Il est parti")]
[(1, 'est', 'verb')]
```

A [`flag_risks()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.flag_risks) `extra` detector: heteronyms whose part of speech picks the reading.

Run it on the *speech* text ([`prepare_speech_text()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text)): a stray verse-initial
capital fools the tagger the same way it fools the speech model.

* **Parameters:**
  * **rules** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `{word: {UPOS tag: reading name}}`, words matched case-insensitively
    (default `FRENCH_POS_HETERONYMS`).
  * **tagger** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `text -> (offset, token, UPOS)`; default [`spacy_tagger()`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.spacy_tagger)
    (French), loaded on first use.
  * **clitics** ([`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Elision clitics (straight apostrophe, lowercase): a risk right after
    one of them (“l’” then “Est”) gets it as its `clitic`; an opening quote
    does not count.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Risk`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.Risk)]]

```pycon
>>> fake = lambda text: [(0, "Il", "PRON"), (3, "est", "AUX"), (7, "parti", "VERB")]
>>> [(r.word, r.expected) for r in pos_detector(tagger=fake)("Il est parti")]
[('est', 'verb')]
>>> fake = lambda text: [(0, "à", "ADP"), (2, "l'", "DET"), (4, "Est", "PROPN")]
>>> [(r.clitic, r.word, r.expected) for r in pos_detector(tagger=fake)("à l'Est")]
[("l'", 'Est', 'noun')]
>>> fake = lambda text: [(0, "'", "PUNCT"), (1, "est", "AUX")]  # a quote, not a clitic
>>> [(r.clitic, r.word) for r in pos_detector(tagger=fake)("'est")]
[('', 'est')]
```

### voxy.speechtext.prepare_speech_text(text, , lowercase_verse_initial=True, keep=(), respellings=None, aliases=None, transforms=())

Display text in, speech text out, with a record of every change.

* **Parameters:**
  * **text** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The text as a reader sees it (lines may be verse lines).
  * **lowercase_verse_initial** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Lowercase a line-initial capital that does not start

  * **keep** ([`Collection`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Collection)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Words whose capital is deliberate and stays (compared exactly). Words
    also capitalised elsewhere in a line are kept automatically.
  * **respellings** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Word -> same-sound spelling, whole words, case-insensitive (e.g.
    a language’s ambiguous forms written unambiguously).
  * **aliases** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Proper name -> pronounceable spelling, whole words, case-insensitive.
  * **transforms** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – Extra `text -> text` steps applied last, over the whole text.
* **Return type:**
  [`SpeechText`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.SpeechText)
* **Returns:**
  A [`SpeechText`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.SpeechText).

### voxy.speechtext.spacy_tagger(model='fr_core_news_sm')

A [`Tagger`](_autosummary/voxy.speechtext.html.md#voxy.speechtext.Tagger) over a spaCy pipeline, loaded on first use.

Needs `pip install 'voxy[pos]'` and the model itself
(`python -m spacy download fr_core_news_sm`).

  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]

### voxy.speechtext.split_clitic(word, clitics)

`(clitic, rest)` of `word` when it starts with one of `clitics` (written
with a straight apostrophe, lowercase), else `("", word)`.

```pycon
>>> split_clitic("L’Est", ("l'",)), split_clitic("c'est", ("l'",))
(('L’', 'Est'), ('', "c'est"))
>>> split_clitic("l'", ("l'",))  # a clitic alone is a word
('', "l'")
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/voxy.splice.html.md

# voxy.splice

Correct words in a recording, in the speaker’s voice: find, render, splice, check.

```pycon
>>> from voxy.splice import replace_words
>>> fixed = replace_words("narration.wav", "Anna Smyth", "Anna Smith",
...                       voice="ada")
>>> fixed.passed, fixed.save("narration-fixed.wav")
```

Replace the whole coarticulated phrase, not one word: a surname spliced alone was
heard with the wrong first consonant, because the first name before it anticipates
the old surname’s lips; replacing first name and surname worked (voxy#38).

Steps, each a seam (keyword argument of `replace_words`):

- `words`: the recording’s timed ASR words (default: `transcriber(audio)`,
  `voxy.refprep.transcribe`); `old` is found among them (`find_phrase`).
- `render(text) -> (samples, sample_rate)`: the new phrase in the voice
  (default `tts_render(voice)`: `voxy.text_to_speech`; a speech-to-speech
  conversion of a spoken correction, or a local clone, plug in the same way).
- The cut lands at the quietest moment near each end of the phrase
  (`cut_points`): in the gap when there is one, and a little past ASR’s word
  times when there is none, since those are often early (a final /z/ left behind
  was heard as “Smith’s”). The render is trimmed, resampled, loudness-matched to
  what it replaces (`level`: by default the RMS of the loud frames on both
  sides, `speech_level`, so pauses do not count), and crossfaded.
- `verify`: checks of the result (default `heard_check`: the new words are
  transcribed where they were put, and the old ones are gone; `voice_check`
  compares the new phrase’s voice print with the rest of the recording’s,
  `voxy.speakers`).

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> sr = 8000
>>> tone = lambda s, amp: amp * np.sin(np.arange(int(s * sr)) / 3).astype(np.float32)
>>> gap = np.zeros(sr // 2)
>>> speech = np.concatenate([tone(1, .3), gap, tone(1, .3), gap, tone(.5, .3)])
>>> words = [{"text": "Hello", "start": 0.0, "end": 1.0},
...          {"text": "Smyth", "start": 1.5, "end": 2.5},
...          {"text": "there.", "start": 3.0, "end": 3.5}]
>>> fixed = replace_words(speech, "smyth", "Smith", words=words, sample_rate=sr,
...                       render=lambda text: (tone(0.8, 0.9), sr), verify=())
>>> fixed.replaced, round(fixed.start, 3), round(fixed.end, 3), fixed.passed
((1.375, 2.625), 1.36, 2.16, None)
```

### voxy.splice.crossfade_join(head, middle, tail, , fade)

`(head + middle + tail, where middle starts in it)`, with linear crossfades
of up to `fade` samples at each join (shorter where a piece is too short; none
at an edge of the audio).

```pycon
>>> joined, at = crossfade_join(np.ones(10), np.ones(6), np.ones(10), fade=2)
>>> len(joined), at
(22, 8)
>>> joined, at = crossfade_join(np.ones(0), np.ones(6), np.ones(10), fade=2)
>>> len(joined), at
(14, 0)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.splice.cut_points(samples, sample_rate, words, first, last, , max_margin=0.25, snap=0.08)

Where to cut (s): the quietest moment before `words[first]` and after
`words[last]`, searched in the gap to the neighbouring word (up to
`max_margin`) and at least `snap` past the ASR boundary. A phrase at an
edge of the audio is cut at that edge.

```pycon
>>> sr, tone = 8000, np.ones(8000)
>>> x = np.concatenate([tone, np.zeros(1600), tone, np.zeros(8000), tone])
>>> ws = [{"start": 0, "end": 1}, {"start": 1.2, "end": 2.2}, {"start": 3.2, "end": 4.2}]
>>> cut_points(x, sr, ws, 1, 1), cut_points(x, sr, ws, 0, 0)[0], cut_points(x, sr, ws, 2, 2)[1]
((1.095, 2.325), 0.0, 4.2)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### voxy.splice.find_phrase(words, phrase, , occurrence=0)

Indices `(first, last)` of the `occurrence`-th run of ASR words saying `phrase`.

```pycon
>>> ws = [{"text": " Anna"}, {"text": " Smyth,"}, {"text": " Anna"}, {"text": " Smyth."}]
>>> find_phrase(ws, "anna smyth"), find_phrase(ws, "Anna … Smyth", occurrence=1)
((0, 1), (2, 3))
```

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.splice.heard_check(, transcriber=None, context=1.0, heard_as=None)

A check: are the new words transcribed where they were spliced in, and the old gone?

`transcriber(wav_path) -> segments` (default `voxy.refprep.transcribe`) runs
on the splice plus `context` seconds each side. `heard_as` is the new phrase
as ASR writes it, when that differs from the text rendered (“Dr. Patterson”
for “Doctor Patterson”); default: the replacement’s `new`. The old phrase
counts as heard only as a whole run of its words (“anna jones”, not “anna”),
and not at all when the new phrase contains it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Replacement`](_autosummary/voxy.splice.html.md#voxy.splice.Replacement)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### voxy.splice.match_loudness(samples, reference, sample_rate, \*, level=<function speech_level>, peak=0.99)

`samples` scaled to `reference`’s `level`, its peak capped at `peak`.

```pycon
>>> x = match_loudness(0.1 * np.ones(160), np.r_[0.5 * np.ones(160), np.zeros(800)], 8000)
>>> round(float(x.max()), 3)
0.5
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.splice.quietest(samples, sample_rate, lo, hi, , tolerance_db=1.0, fallback=None)

The time (s) of the quietest frame in `[lo, hi]`; of equally quiet frames
(within `tolerance_db`), the one nearest the middle of the window. When no
frame lies there (an empty window, or one past the last full frame):
`fallback`, default `lo`.

```pycon
>>> x = np.concatenate([np.ones(800), np.zeros(800), np.ones(800)])
>>> quietest(x, 8000, 0.0, 0.3)
0.145
>>> quietest(x, 8000, 0.3, 0.3), quietest(x, 8000, 0.3, 0.35, fallback=0.31)
(0.3, 0.31)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### voxy.splice.replace_words(audio, old, new, \*, voice=None, render=None, words=None, transcriber=None, sample_rate=None, occurrence=0, crossfade_ms=15, max_margin_ms=250, snap_ms=80, level=<function speech_level>, verify=None)

Replace the spoken phrase `old` with `new`, rendered in `voice`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **audio** – A WAV path or bytes (channels averaged), or raw mono samples (with
    `sample_rate=`; integer PCM is scaled to `[-1, 1)`).
  * **old** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The phrase as spoken (several words: see the module docstring).
  * **new** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What it should say.
  * **voice** – The speaker’s voice, for the default `render` (a library name, a
    backend voice, a profile). `voice` or `render` is required.
  * **render** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `text -> (samples, sample_rate)`; default `tts_render(voice)`.
    A render that is silent raises `ValueError`.
  * **words** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Timed ASR words of `audio`; default `transcriber(audio)`.
  * **transcriber** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – `wav_path -> segments` (default `voxy.refprep.transcribe`),
    for `words` and the default check.
  * **occurrence** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – Which occurrence of `old` (0: the first).
  * **crossfade_ms** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – Length of each crossfade.
  * **max_margin_ms** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – The furthest a cut may sit from the phrase, in a gap.
  * **snap_ms** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)) – How far past an ASR boundary a cut may look for quiet.
  * **level** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – `(samples, sample_rate) -> level` the render is matched on;
    default `speech_level` (e.g. `partial(speech_level, margin_db=10)`).
  * **verify** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Replacement`](_autosummary/voxy.splice.html.md#voxy.splice.Replacement)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)] | [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Replacement`](_autosummary/voxy.splice.html.md#voxy.splice.Replacement)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – A check or checks (`(samples, sample_rate, replacement) -> dict`
    with a `passed` key); default `heard_check`; `()` for none.
* **Return type:**
  [`Replacement`](_autosummary/voxy.splice.html.md#voxy.splice.Replacement)

### voxy.splice.speech_level(samples, sample_rate, , margin_db=20.0)

RMS of the loud frames (within `margin_db` of the loudest), so that pauses
do not lower it; plain RMS when there is no full frame.

```pycon
>>> x = np.concatenate([0.5 * np.ones(800), np.zeros(8000)])
>>> round(speech_level(x, 8000), 3), round(float(np.sqrt(np.mean(x**2))), 3)
(0.5, 0.151)
```

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

### voxy.splice.tts_render(voice=None, , backend=None, voices=None, use_library=True, model=None, \*\*tts_kwargs)

A `render` speaking the text with `voxy.text_to_speech` in `voice`.

The voice is resolved once, here (`voxy.facade.resolve_voice`, with
`voices`, `use_library` and `model`’s backend), and every render
synthesizes with what it resolved to. Backends whose default output is
compressed get a WAV/PCM format (`DFLT_RENDER_FORMATS`) unless
`output_format=` is given; other `tts_kwargs` go to `text_to_speech`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]]

### voxy.splice.voice_check(, embed=None, min_similarity=None, window=None)

A check: does the new phrase sound like the rest of the recording’s speaker?

Cosine similarity of the voice print of the new phrase and of the rest
(`voxy.speakers.voice_print`, ECAPA in its own environment unless `embed`
is given). `min_similarity` defaults to `speakers.DFLT_MATCH_SIMILARITY`
(below it, a window counts as someone else); `window` (s) defaults to the
speakers’ window, shortened to the phrase. Fails, with a `reason`, when the
new phrase is the whole recording.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int), [`Replacement`](_autosummary/voxy.splice.html.md#voxy.splice.Replacement)], [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]


# _autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md

# voxy.stores

Where voxy keeps its data: voice records and audio, as `MutableMapping` stores.

Layout under the data root (`$VOXY_DATA_DIR`, default `~/.local/share/voxy`
via `config2py`), one subfolder per kind of data:

> voices/{name}.json        voice records: aliases, consent, one profile per backend
> samples/{name}/{file}     prepared audio a clone is made from
> sources/{name}/{file}     raw source media the samples were cut from

Callers take a store as an argument (`voices=`, `samples=`) and never build
paths themselves, so moving the data elsewhere (another folder, S3, a database)
means passing a different `MutableMapping`. Folders are created on first write.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> voices = voices_store(rootdir=root)
>>> voices["ada"] = {"name": "ada"}
>>> list(voices), voices["ada"]
(['ada'], {'name': 'ada'})
>>> samples = samples_store("ada", rootdir=root)
>>> samples["clip.wav"] = b"RIFF"
>>> list(samples)
['clip.wav']
```

### Functions

| [`audio_store`](_autosummary/voxy.stores.html.md#voxy.stores.audio_store)(kind, voice, \*[, rootdir])   | Audio files of one voice and kind, `filename -> bytes`.                           |

# _autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md

# voxy.textsplit

Split long text (a chapter) into chunks a speech model can say in one breath.

Local cloning models drift, rush or hallucinate past roughly 20-40 seconds of
speech, so long text is spoken chunk by chunk and the audio joined with
controlled pauses. Paragraphs are kept apart (they get a longer pause); inside a
paragraph, whole sentences are packed into chunks of at most `max_chars`, and
only a sentence longer than that is cut, at a clause break if it has one.

```pycon
>>> split_text("One. Two!\n\nThree is a longer sentence, with a clause.", max_chars=20)
[['One. Two!'], ['Three is a longer', 'sentence,', 'with a clause.']]
```

### Module Attributes

| [`ABBREVIATIONS`](_autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md#voxy.textsplit.ABBREVIATIONS)   | Words ending in a period that don't end a sentence ("Mr.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------|

|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`split_text`](_autosummary/voxy.textsplit.html.md#voxy.textsplit.split_text)(text, \*[, max_chars]) | Paragraphs of chunks: `[[chunk, ...], ...]`, each chunk at most `max_chars`. |

# _autosummary/voxy.voicestudio_model.html.md

# voxy.voicestudio_model

Local description-prompted speech through VoiceStudio (Parler-TTS and friends).

A voice here is a *text description* (“a warm, low female voice, close to the
microphone”), not a recording: `voice` may be that string or a `VoiceProfile`
made by `design_voice`. Nothing is uploaded; weights run locally (CPU works,
slowly) and are fetched from Hugging Face on first use (`model_id=`; the default
is several GB, so `pip install 'voxy[voicestudio]'` does not download them).

The model call is a seam: `generate(text, description) -> (waveform, sample_rate)`
is injectable, so tests (and other VoiceStudio architectures) never load weights.

```pycon
>>> model = VoiceStudioSpeechModel(generate=lambda text, description: ([0.0] * 8, 8000))
>>> model.synthesize("Hi", "a calm voice").format
'wav'
```

### Classes

| [`VoiceStudioSpeechModel`](_autosummary/voxy.voicestudio_model.html.md#voxy.voicestudio_model.VoiceStudioSpeechModel)(\*[, model_id, ...])   | VoiceStudio (description-prompted TTS) as a voxy backend.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|

# _autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md

# voxy.wavutil

Mono PCM WAV in and out as float arrays, plus the few edits narration needs.

Every local backend and the reference-prep step exchange 16-bit PCM WAV files;
this module turns them into `float32` arrays in `[-1, 1]` and back, trims
silence, and joins pieces with pauses, using only numpy and the standard library.

```pycon
>>> import numpy as np
>>> data = write_wav(np.array([0.0, 0.5, -0.5], dtype=np.float32), 8000)
>>> samples, sr = read_wav(data)
>>> sr, np.round(samples, 3).tolist()
(8000, [0.0, 0.5, -0.5])
```

### Module Attributes

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`WAVE_FORMAT_FLOAT`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.WAVE_FORMAT_FLOAT)      | integer PCM, IEEE float, and the extensible wrapper.                       |
| [`WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE) | integer PCM, IEEE float, and the extensible wrapper.                       |
| [`TRAILING_CHUNK_IDS`](_autosummary/voxy.wavutil.html.md#voxy.wavutil.TRAILING_CHUNK_IDS)     | Chunks that can follow audio whose `data` size is a streaming placeholder. |

```pycon

[-100.0, -100.0]
```

### voxy.wavutil.pcm_to_float(raw, width=2)

Little-endian PCM samples of `width` bytes as floats in about `[-1, 1]`
(the most negative sample is a hair below -1).

8-bit PCM is unsigned (silence is 128); a trailing partial sample (a stream cut
mid-sample) is dropped.

```pycon
>>> pcm_to_float(b"\x00\x00\xff\x7f\x01").tolist()
[0.0, 1.0]
>>> pcm_to_float(bytes([0, 128, 255]), 1).tolist()
[-1.0, 0.0, 0.9921875]
>>> pcm_to_float(bytes([0xFF, 0xFF, 0x7F, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80]), 3).tolist()
[1.0, -1.0000001192092896]
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.wavutil.read_wav(source)

`(samples, sample_rate)` of a WAV (path or bytes), channels averaged.

Integer PCM (8, 16, 24, 32 bit) and 32-bit float, plain or extensible headers,
and streamed files whose header carries a placeholder size (the audio then ends
at a trailing chunk such as `LIST`, or at the end of the file).

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[`ndarray`, [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### voxy.wavutil.resample(samples, from_rate, to_rate)

Linear-interpolation resampling (enough to join pieces; use ffmpeg for masters).

```pycon
>>> len(resample(np.zeros(100), 8000, 16000))
200
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.wavutil.silence(ms, sample_rate)

`ms` milliseconds of silence.

```pycon
>>> len(silence(250, 8000))
2000
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

### voxy.wavutil.trim_silence(samples, sample_rate, , threshold_db=-45.0, keep_ms=60)

Drop leading and trailing frames quieter than `threshold_db` (keeping `keep_ms`).

```pycon
>>> x = np.concatenate([np.zeros(800), 0.5 * np.ones(800), np.zeros(800)])
>>> len(trim_silence(x, 8000, keep_ms=0))
800
```

* **Return type:**
  `ndarray`

# _autosummary/voxy.worker.html.md

# voxy.worker

Talk to a model running in another Python environment, as if it were local.

`Worker` starts `voxy/workers/serve.py` with an environment’s interpreter,
keeps it alive (weights load once), and turns each call into one JSON line each
way. Its stderr (model logs, progress bars) goes to a log file, so a chatty
library can’t fill a pipe and hang the call.

```pycon
>>> import sys, tempfile, pathlib
>>> adapter = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / "echo_adapter.py"
>>> _ = adapter.write_text("def load(**kw): return kw\ndef echo(state, **kw): return {**state, **kw}")
>>> with Worker(sys.executable, adapter, init={"a": 1}) as w:
...     w.call("echo", b=2)
{'a': 1, 'b': 2}
```

### Functions

| [`env_worker`](_autosummary/voxy.worker.html.md#voxy.worker.env_worker)(spec, adapter, \*[, model, init, ...])   | A worker for adapter `adapter` in `spec`'s environment, its log `logs/<adapter>.log` under voxy's cache: the one place an environment and an adapter become a worker.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Worker`](_autosummary/voxy.worker.html.md#voxy.worker.Worker)(python, adapter, \*[, init, env, ...])   | A long-lived adapter process: `call(op, **request) -> dict`.                                                                                                                        |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`WorkerPool`](_autosummary/voxy.worker.html.md#voxy.worker.WorkerPool)(spec, adapter, \*[, make])           | Shared workers of one adapter, one per `(model, threads, rootdir)`, each made once even when threads ask for it at the same time (so its environment is never built twice at once). |

### Exceptions

| [`WorkerError`](_autosummary/voxy.worker.html.md#voxy.worker.WorkerError)   | An operation failed inside the worker (the message carries its traceback tail).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* voxy.worker.Worker(python, adapter, , init=None, env=None, log_path=None, cwd=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A long-lived adapter process: `call(op, **request) -> dict`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **python** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – Interpreter of the environment to run in.
  * **adapter** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike)) – The adapter file (`load` plus operations).
  * **init** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Keyword arguments for the adapter’s `load` (sent on start).
  * **env** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Environment variables of the process (default: inherited).
  * **log_path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Where the process’s stderr goes (default: a temp file).
  * **cwd** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`PathLike`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.PathLike) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – Working directory (default: a neutral temp dir, so nothing in the
    caller’s folder shadows the environment’s imports).

#### call(op, \*\*request)

Run `op` in the worker (starting it, and loading the model, on first use).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

#### close()

Stop the process (its memory goes back to the machine).

From another thread, this waits for a call in flight to finish first, so it
cannot abort a hung call (a separate `kill` would be needed for that).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### *property* running *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

True while the process is alive.

# voxy.workers

Backend adapters run by `voxy.worker` inside each backend’s own environment.

`serve.py` is the entry point; each `*_adapter.py` wraps one model library
with `load(**init)` and `synthesize(state, *, text, ref_audio, ref_text,
out_path, \*\*params)`. These files are executed by other interpreters, so they
import nothing from voxy.

### Functions

| [`adapter_path`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.html.md#voxy.workers.adapter_path)(name)   | The adapter file for `name` (e.g. 'f5tts' -> `f5tts_adapter.py`).   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|

### voxy.workers.adapter_path(name)

The adapter file for `name` (e.g. ‘f5tts’ -> `f5tts_adapter.py`).

```pycon
>>> adapter_path("f5tts").name
'f5tts_adapter.py'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### Modules

| [`asr_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.asr_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.asr_adapter)               | Speech recognition with timed words (scribed's faster-whisper backend), for reference prep.                                                       |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`chatterbox_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.chatterbox_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.chatterbox_adapter) | Chatterbox (Resemble AI): 'original' (emotion exaggeration, CFG), 'turbo' (faster), or 'multilingual' (23 languages; pass `language`, e.g. 'fr'). |
| [`f5tts_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.f5tts_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.f5tts_adapter)           | F5-TTS (flow matching, zero-shot cloning from a reference clip and its text).                                                                     |
| [`kokoro_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.kokoro_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.kokoro_adapter)         | Kokoro-82M through kokoro-onnx: stock voices on CPU, no torch, no reference clip.                                                                 |
| [`phonemes_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.phonemes_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.phonemes_adapter)     | Phoneme recognition (wav2vec2 espeak CTC): frame-wise log-probabilities of a crop, and espeak phonemization.                                      |
| [`qwen3tts_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.qwen3tts_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.qwen3tts_adapter)     | Qwen3-TTS (Alibaba Qwen): Base voice cloning from a clip and its text (ICL mode), and VoiceDesign (a voice from a description).                   |
| [`serve`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.serve.html.md#module-voxy.workers.serve)                           | Worker entry point: run a backend adapter inside its own environment.                                                                             |
| [`speaker_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.speaker_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.speaker_adapter)       | Speaker embeddings (SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN) of sliding windows, for speaker filtering.                                                            |
| [`voxcpm_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.voxcpm_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.voxcpm_adapter)         | VoxCPM2 (OpenBMB): tokenizer-free diffusion-autoregressive cloning, 48 kHz output.                                                                |
| [`xtts_adapter`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.xtts_adapter.html.md#module-voxy.workers.xtts_adapter)             | XTTS-v2 (Coqui, maintained by idiap as coqui-tts): GPT-style cloning from a short clip.                                                           |


# _autosummary/voxy.workers.kokoro_adapter.html.md

# voxy.workers.kokoro_adapter

Kokoro-82M through kokoro-onnx: stock voices on CPU, no torch, no reference clip.

The model files come from the Hugging Face hub (`hf_hub_download`, cached under
`$HF_HOME`, which voxy sets for every worker); which repo, revision and files is
the caller’s `init` (`voxy.kokoro_model.KOKORO`). onnxruntime ignores
`OMP_NUM_THREADS`, so its thread pool is capped here from `$VOXY_NUM_THREADS`.

### Functions

| `load`(\*, repo_id, revision, model_file, ...)       |    |
|------------------------------------------------------|----|
| `synthesize`(state, \*, text, voice, out_path, lang) |    |

# _autosummary/voxy.workers.serve.html.md

# voxy.workers.serve

Worker entry point: run a backend adapter inside its own environment.

Started by `voxy.worker.Worker` with the environment’s interpreter, as
`python serve.py <adapter.py>`. It imports nothing from voxy (the environment
need not have voxy installed), loads the adapter file, then answers one JSON
request per stdin line with one JSON reply per line on the original stdout.
Everything the model libraries print goes to stderr (the worker’s log), so it
can’t corrupt the replies.

An adapter is a plain module with `load(**init) -> state` and any number of
operations `op(state, **request) -> dict` (JSON-ready), e.g. `synthesize`.
Request: `{"op": "load", ...}` or `{"op": "<name>", ...}`.
Reply: `{"ok": true, "result": {...}}` or `{"ok": false, "error": "...", "traceback": "..."}`.

### Functions

| `main`([argv])   |    |
|------------------|----|


# _autosummary/voxy.workers.speaker_adapter.html.md

# voxy.workers.speaker_adapter

Speaker embeddings (SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN) of sliding windows, for speaker filtering.

### Functions

| [`embed`](_autosummary/voxy.workers.speaker_adapter.html.md#voxy.workers.speaker_adapter.embed)(state, \*, audio, out_path[, spans, ...])   | Embed windows of `window` s every `hop` s inside `spans` (default: all).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `load`(\*[, model, device])                                                                        |                                                                            |

### voxy.workers.speaker_adapter.embed(state, , audio, out_path, spans=None, window=1.0, hop=0.1, batch=64)

Embed windows of `window` s every `hop` s inside `spans` (default: all).

Saves `times` (n, 2) and unit `vectors` (n, d) to the `.npz` `out_path`.
A span shorter than `window` gets one window, its own length.

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`voxy` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `voxy`

Read first whenever spoken voice must be generated - “use voice X to…”, “use a cloned voice for…”, “have X narrate…”, “say/read this in X’s voice”, voice-over, dubbing, giving characters voices, text-to-speech, which voices we have, cloning or designing a voice - and when making a video, animation, podcast or demo where a character or narrator speaks. voxy is the fleet’s voice-generation facade; never call a TTS SDK directly.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/voxy voxy --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`voxy/data/skills/voxy`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/voxy/tree/HEAD/voxy/data/skills/voxy) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install voxy`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/voxy/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/voxy/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`voxy.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/voxy/voxy.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/voxy/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
